title.zh: 卷四百九十 列傳第二百四十九 外國六 天竺 于闐 高昌 回鶻 大食 層檀 龜茲 沙州 拂菻
title.en: Volume 490 Biographies 249: Foreign States 6: India, Yutian, Gaochang, Huihu, Dashi, Cengtan, Kezil, Dunhuang, Byzantine Empire
title.raw: 卷四百九十 列傳第二百四十九 外國六 天竺 于闐 高昌 回鶻 大食 層檀 龜茲 沙州 拂菻 Volume 490 Biographies 249: Foreign States 6: India, Yutian, Gaochang, Huihu, Dashi, Cengtan, Kezil, Dunhuang, Byzantine Empire

sentences.zh: 外國六○天竺于闐高昌回鶻大食層檀龜茲沙州拂菻

translations.literal: Foreign States 6: India, Yutian, Gaochang, Huihu, Dashi, Cengtan, Kucha, Shazhou, Fulin.
translations.idiomatic: Foreign States 6 — India, Khotan, Gaochang, the Uyghurs, Dashi, Cengtan, Kucha, Shazhou, and Byzantium.

sentences.zh: 天竺國舊名身毒，亦曰摩伽陀，復曰婆羅門。

translations.literal: The state of Tianzhu was formerly called Shendu; it is also called Magadha, and again called Brahmana.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom of India was formerly known as Shendu; it was also called Magadha, and is likewise known as Brahmana.

sentences.zh: 俗宗浮圖道，不飲酒食肉。

translations.literal: The custom is to revere the Buddhist Way; they do not drink wine or eat meat.
translations.idiomatic: The people follow Buddhism and abstain from wine and meat.

sentences.zh: 漢武帝遣使十餘輩間出西南，指求身毒，為昆明所閉，莫能通。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Han sent more than ten envoys who went out by separate routes through the southwest, seeking Shendu; they were blocked by Kunming and could not get through.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Han dispatched more than a dozen envoys by different routes through the southwest in search of India, but the Kunming people barred their way and none could reach it.

sentences.zh: 至漢明帝夢金人，於是遣使天竺問佛道法，由是其教傳於中國。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming of Han dreamed of a golden man, he then sent envoys to Tianzhu to inquire about Buddhist doctrine and law, and thereby that teaching spread in China.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming of Han dreamed of a golden figure, he sent envoys to India to inquire into Buddhist teaching, and from that time the faith spread in China.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝、後魏宣武時，皆來貢獻。

translations.literal: In the times of Emperor Wu of Liang and Emperor Xuanwu of Later Wei, they all came to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: During the reigns of Emperor Wu of Liang and Emperor Xuanwu of Northern Wei, they sent tribute missions.

sentences.zh: 隋煬帝誌通西域，諸國多有至者，唯天竺不通。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang of Sui desired to open the Western Regions; many states came, but only Tianzhu did not connect.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang of Sui sought to open contact with the Western Regions; many states sent envoys, but India alone remained unreachable.

sentences.zh: 唐貞觀以後，朝貢相繼。

translations.literal: After the Zhenguan era of Tang, court tribute followed in succession.
translations.idiomatic: After the Zhenguan reign of Tang, tribute missions arrived in steady succession.

sentences.zh: 則天天授中，五天竺王並來朝獻。

translations.literal: In the Tianshou era of Empress Wu Zetian, the kings of the Five Indias all came to court to present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianshou era of Empress Wu, the rulers of all five Indias came to court with tribute.

sentences.zh: 乾元末，河隴陷沒，遂不復至。

translations.literal: At the end of the Qianyuan era, the He and Long regions fell; thereafter they did not come again.
translations.idiomatic: When the He and Long circuits were lost at the end of the Qianyuan era, the missions ceased.

sentences.zh: 周廣順三年，西天竺僧薩滿多等十六族來貢名馬。

translations.literal: In the third year of Guangshun of Zhou, the monk Samanduo of Western Tianzhu and sixteen clans came to present famous horses.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Guangshun of Later Zhou, the Western Indian monk Samanduo and envoys from sixteen clans presented fine horses.

sentences.zh: 乾德三年，滄州僧道圓自西域還，得佛舍利一水晶器、貝葉梵經四十夾來獻。

translations.literal: In the third year of Qiande, the monk Daoyuan of Cangzhou returned from the Western Regions, obtained one crystal vessel of Buddhist relics and forty bundles of palm-leaf Sanskrit scriptures, and came to present them.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Qiande, the Cangzhou monk Daoyuan returned from the west bearing a crystal reliquary of Buddhist relics and forty bundles of palm-leaf sutras, which he presented at court.

sentences.zh: 道圓晉天福中詣西域，在塗十二年，住五印度凡六年，五印度即天竺也；

translations.literal: Daoyuan went to the Western Regions in the Tianfu era of Jin; on the road twelve years, he stayed in the Five Indias altogether six years — the Five Indias are Tianzhu.
translations.idiomatic: Daoyuan had set out for the Western Regions in the Tianfu era of Later Jin; he was twelve years on the road and spent six years in the Five Indias — that is, India.

sentences.zh: 還經于闐，與其使偕至。

translations.literal: Returning he passed through Yutian and arrived together with its envoy.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he passed through Khotan and arrived together with that kingdom's embassy.

sentences.zh: 太祖召問所曆風俗山川道里，一一能記。

translations.literal: The Taizu Emperor summoned him to ask about the customs, mountains and rivers, and routes he had seen; he could record each one.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu questioned him about the customs, geography, and routes he had seen, and he could recount them all in detail.

sentences.zh: 四年，僧行勤等一百五十七人詣闕上言，願至西域求佛書，許之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, the monks Xingqin and others, one hundred fifty-seven persons, went to the palace gate and petitioned, wishing to go to the Western Regions to seek Buddhist books; this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, one hundred fifty-seven monks led by Xingqin petitioned the throne to travel west for Buddhist scriptures, and permission was granted.

sentences.zh: 以其所曆甘、沙、伊、肅等州，焉耆、龜茲、于闐、割祿等國，又曆布路沙、加濕彌羅等國，並詔諭其國令人引導之。

translations.literal: Because they would pass through the prefectures Gan, Sha, Yi, and Su, and the states Yanqi, Kucha, Yutian, Gelu, and also Buluosha, Kashmir, and other states, edicts were sent to instruct those states to provide guides.
translations.idiomatic: Edicts were sent to Gan, Sha, Yi, Su, and to Yanqi, Kucha, Khotan, Gelu, Buluosha, Kashmir, and other states along their route, ordering local authorities to provide guides.

sentences.zh: 開寶後，天竺僧持梵夾來獻者不絕。

translations.literal: After the Kaibao era, Tianzhu monks presenting Sanskrit bundles did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: After the Kaibao era, Indian monks bearing Sanskrit manuscripts presented them at court without interruption.

sentences.zh: 八年冬，東印度王子穰結說囉來朝貢。

translations.literal: In the winter of the eighth year, the Eastern Indian prince Rangjieshuoluo came to court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the eighth year, the Eastern Indian prince Rangjieshuoluo arrived at court with tribute.

sentences.zh: 天竺之法，國王死，太子襲位，餘子皆出家為僧，不復居本國。

translations.literal: By Tianzhu law, when the king dies the crown prince succeeds; the other sons all leave home to become monks and no longer dwell in their native state.
translations.idiomatic: By Indian custom, when the king died the crown prince succeeded, while his other sons took monastic vows and left the realm.

sentences.zh: 有曼殊室利者，乃其王子也，隨中國僧至焉，太祖令館於相國寺，善持律，為都人之所傾向，財施盈室。

translations.literal: There was one Manjushri, who was a prince of that land; he had come with Chinese monks. The Taizu Emperor ordered him lodged at Xiangguo Temple; he was skilled in keeping the vinaya, and the people of the capital inclined toward him; offerings of wealth filled his rooms.
translations.idiomatic: One Manjushri, a prince of that land, had come with Chinese monks. Taizu lodged him at Xiangguo Temple. He was a skilled vinaya master whom the capital greatly admired, and donations filled his quarters.

sentences.zh: 眾僧頗嫉之，以其不解唐言，即偽為奏求還本國，許之。

translations.literal: The monks were rather jealous of him; because he did not understand Tang speech, they forged a memorial asking that he return to his native land, and this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The clergy grew jealous of him and, since he did not understand Chinese, forged a petition for his repatriation, which was approved.

sentences.zh: 詔既下，曼殊室利始大驚恨，眾僧諭以詔旨，不得已遲留數月而後去。

translations.literal: Once the edict was issued, Manjushri was greatly shocked and resentful; the monks explained the edict's intent, and he had no choice but to delay several months before departing.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict arrived, Manjushri was deeply dismayed. The monks explained its terms, and he lingered reluctantly for several months before leaving.

sentences.zh: 自言詣南海附賈人船而歸，終不知所適。

translations.literal: He said himself that he would go to the Southern Sea and take passage on a merchant ship to return; in the end no one knew where he went.
translations.idiomatic: He said he would sail from the southern coast on a merchant vessel homeward, but his final destination was never known.

sentences.zh: 太平興國七年，益州僧光遠至自天竺，以其王沒徙曩表來上。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Taiping Xingguo, the Yizhou monk Guangyuan arrived from Tianzhu, presenting the memorial of his king Motuoxiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Taiping Xingguo, the Yizhou monk Guangyuan arrived from India bearing a memorial from King Motuoxiang.

sentences.zh: 上令天竺僧施護譯云：「近聞支那國內有大明王，至聖至明，威力自在。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the Tianzhu monk Shihu to translate: "Recently I have heard that within the land of Zhina there is a great Illumined King, supremely holy and supremely bright, whose power is free.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had the Indian monk Shihu translate: "We have lately heard that in the land of China there reigns a great Illumined King, supremely holy and wise, whose power is absolute.

sentences.zh: 每慚薄幸，朝謁無由，遙望支那起居聖躬萬福。

translations.literal: I am ever ashamed of my slight fortune, with no means to attend court; gazing from afar toward Zhina, I wish Your Sacred Person ten thousand blessings.
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed of our meager fortune, we have had no means to attend your court; from afar we wish Your Majesty long life and boundless blessing.

sentences.zh: 光遠來，蒙賜金剛吉祥無畏坐釋迦聖像袈裟一事，已披掛供養。

translations.literal: Guangyuan has come; we received the gift of one kāṣāya for the sacred image of Śākyamuni on the Vajra Auspicious Fearless Throne, and it has already been draped and offered in worship.
translations.idiomatic: Through Guangyuan we received the kāṣāya for the image of Śākyamuni upon the Vajra Auspicious Fearless Throne, and it has been draped upon the statue in worship.

sentences.zh: 伏願支那皇帝福慧圓滿，壽命延長，常為引導一切有情生死海中，渡諸沉溺。

translations.literal: I humbly pray that the emperor of Zhina may have blessings and wisdom complete, life prolonged, and ever guide all sentient beings in the sea of birth and death, ferrying those who are drowning.
translations.idiomatic: We pray that the emperor of China may enjoy perfect merit and wisdom, long life, and that he may forever guide all beings across the sea of birth and death and rescue the drowning.

sentences.zh: 今以釋迦舍利附光遠上進。」

translations.literal: Now I send Śākyamuni's relics with Guangyuan to present upward."
translations.idiomatic: We now send relics of the Buddha with Guangyuan as our tribute."

sentences.zh: 又譯其國僧統表，詞意亦與沒徙曩同。

translations.literal: He also translated the memorial of the sangha superintendent of that land; its wording and meaning were likewise the same as Motuoxiang's."
translations.idiomatic: He also translated a memorial from that kingdom's chief of the sangha, whose wording matched Motuoxiang's.

sentences.zh: 施護者，烏塤曩國人。

translations.literal: Shihu was a man of the state of Udyana.
translations.idiomatic: Shihu was a native of Udyana.

sentences.zh: 其國屬北印度，西行十二日至乾陀羅國，又西行二十日至曩誐囉賀囉國，又西行十日至嵐婆國，又西行十二日至誐惹曩國，又西行至波斯國，得西海。

translations.literal: That state belonged to North India; westward twelve days to Gandhara, again west twenty days to Nagarahara, again west ten days to Lambaka, again west twelve days to Gurjara, again westward to Persia, reaching the Western Sea.
translations.idiomatic: His country lay in North India. Westward twelve days brought one to Gandhara; twenty days farther to Nagarahara; ten days farther to Lambaka; twelve days farther to Gurjara; and still farther west to Persia and the Western Sea.

sentences.zh: 自北印度行百二十日至中印度。

translations.literal: From North India, traveling one hundred twenty days reached Central India.
translations.idiomatic: From North India it was one hundred twenty days' journey to Central India.

sentences.zh: 中印度西行三程至嗬囉尾國，又西行十二日至未曩囉國，又西行十二日至缽賴野迦國，又西行六十日至迦囉拿俱惹國，又西行二十日至摩囉尾國，又西行二十日至烏然泥國，又西行二十五日至囉囉國，又西行四十日至蘇囉茶國，又西行十一日至西海。

translations.literal: From Central India west three stages to Harivari, again west twelve days to Malava, again west twelve days to Bharukaccha, again west sixty days to Karanayuja, again west twenty days to Maru, again west twenty days to Ujjayini, again west twenty-five days to Lala, again west forty days to Surashtra, again west eleven days to the Western Sea.
translations.idiomatic: From Central India, three stages west lay Harivari; twelve days farther, Malava; twelve days farther, Bharukaccha; sixty days farther, Karanayuja; twenty days farther, Maru; twenty days farther, Ujjayini; twenty-five days farther, Lala; forty days farther, Surashtra; and eleven days farther to the Western Sea.

sentences.zh: 自中印度行六月程至南印度，又西行九十日至供迦拿國，又西行一月至海。

translations.literal: From Central India, six months' journey reached South India; again west ninety days to Konkana, again west one month to the sea.
translations.idiomatic: From Central India it was six months to South India; ninety days farther west to Konkana; and one month farther to the sea.

sentences.zh: 自南印度南行六月程得南海。

translations.literal: From South India, south six months' journey reached the Southern Sea.
translations.idiomatic: From South India, six months south brought one to the Southern Sea.

sentences.zh: 皆施護之所述雲。

translations.literal: All this was as Shihu described.
translations.idiomatic: Such were the routes Shihu described.

sentences.zh: 八年，僧法遇自天竺取經回，至三佛齊，遇天竺僧彌摩羅失黎語不多命，附表願至中國譯經，上優詔召之。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, the monk Fayu returned from fetching scriptures in Tianzhu; reaching Srivijaya, he met the Tianzhu monk Mimiluoshili, whose command of speech was not great; he attached a memorial wishing to come to China to translate scriptures, and the emperor issued a gracious edict summoning him.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year the monk Fayu returned from India with scriptures. At Srivijaya he met the Indian monk Mimiluoshili, who spoke little Chinese but sent a memorial asking to come to China to translate scriptures; the emperor graciously summoned him.

sentences.zh: 法遇後募緣製龍寶蓋袈裟，將復往天竺，表乞給所經諸國敕書，遂賜三佛齊國王遐至葛、古羅國主司馬佶芒、柯蘭國主讚怛羅、西天王子謨馱仙書以遣之。

translations.literal: Fayu later raised funds to make a dragon-jeweled-canopy kāṣāya and was about to go again to Tianzhu; he memorialized asking letters of instruction for the states he would pass through, and thereupon were granted letters to the king of Srivijaya Xiage, the lord of Gulu Sima Jiemang, the lord of Kalan Zhandaluo, and the Western Heaven prince Mo Tuoxian to send with him.
translations.idiomatic: Fayu later raised funds for a dragon-canopy kāṣāya and prepared to return to India, requesting imperial letters for the states along his route. Letters were granted to the king of Srivijaya, the ruler of Gulu, the lord of Kalan, and the Western Heaven prince Mo Tuoxian.

sentences.zh: 雍熙中，衛州僧辭瀚自西域還，與胡僧密坦羅奉北印度王及金剛坐王那爛陀書來。

translations.literal: In the Yongxi era, the Weizhou monk Cihan returned from the Western Regions, and with the foreign monk Mitanluo presented letters from the king of North India and the Diamond Throne king of Nalanda.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongxi era the Weizhou monk Cihan returned from the west with the foreign monk Mitanluo, bearing letters from the king of North India and the Diamond Throne king of Nalanda.

sentences.zh: 又有婆羅門僧永世與波斯外道阿裏煙同至京師。

translations.literal: There were also the Brahman monk Yongshi and the Persian non-Buddhist Aliyan who arrived together at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The Brahman monk Yongshi and the Persian lay teacher Aliyan also arrived at the capital together.

sentences.zh: 永世自云：本國名利得，國王姓牙羅五得，名阿喏你縛，衣黃衣，戴金冠，以七寶為飾。

translations.literal: Yongshi said himself: "In my native land called Lide, the king's surname is Yarowude, his name Anuoniwa; he wears yellow robes and a golden crown adorned with the seven jewels."
translations.idiomatic: Yongshi said that in his homeland, called Lide, the king bore the surname Yarowude and the name Anuoniwa, wore yellow robes, and wore a golden crown set with the seven jewels.

sentences.zh: 出乘象或肩輿，以音樂螺鈸前導，多遊佛寺，博施貧乏。

translations.literal: Going out he rides an elephant or a palanquin; music of conches and cymbals leads before him; he often visits Buddhist temples and broadly bestows on the poor.
translations.idiomatic: When he went abroad he rode an elephant or a palanquin, preceded by conches and cymbals; he often visited monasteries and gave generously to the poor.

sentences.zh: 其妃曰摩訶你，衣大紬縷金紅衣，歲一出，多所振施。

translations.literal: His consort is called Moheni; she wears great brocade with gold thread and red robes; once a year she goes out and bestows much in relief.
translations.idiomatic: His consort, called Moheni, wore great brocade robes threaded with gold and crimson; once a year she went abroad and distributed lavish charity.

sentences.zh: 人有冤抑，候王及妃出遊，即迎隨伸訴。

translations.literal: If people had grievances suppressed, they waited until the king and consort went out on tour, then went forward following them to state their complaints.
translations.idiomatic: Those with grievances waited until the king and queen went abroad, then approached them to plead their cases.

sentences.zh: 署國相四人，庶務並委裁制。

translations.literal: He appointed four chief ministers of state; all routine affairs were entrusted to their judgment and decision.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed four chief ministers, to whom all routine affairs were entrusted.

sentences.zh: 五穀、六畜、果實與中國無異。

translations.literal: The five grains, six domestic animals, and fruits were no different from China.
translations.idiomatic: Grain, livestock, and fruit were the same as in China.

sentences.zh: 市易用銅錢，有文漫圓徑，如中國之制，但實其中心，不穿貫耳。

translations.literal: Market exchange used copper coins with characters around the circumference, like China's system, but solid in the center, without a hole for stringing.
translations.idiomatic: Trade used copper coins inscribed around the rim like China's, but solid in the center without a hole for stringing.

sentences.zh: 其國東行經六月至大食國，又二月至西州，又三月至夏州。

translations.literal: Eastward from that state, six months reached Dashi; again two months to Xizhou; again three months to Xiazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Eastward from his country it was six months to Dashi, two months more to Xizhou, and three months more to Xiazhou.

sentences.zh: 阿裏煙自云：本國王號黑衣，姓張，名哩沒，用錦彩為衣，每遊獵，三二日一還國。

translations.literal: Aliyan said himself: "In my native land the king is called the Black Robe; his surname Zhang, his name Limo; he uses brocade for clothing; whenever he goes hunting, he returns to the state every two or three days."
translations.idiomatic: Aliyan said that in his land the king was called the Black Robe, bore the surname Zhang and the name Limo, dressed in brocade, and when hunting returned home every two or three days.

sentences.zh: 署大臣九人治國事。

translations.literal: He appointed nine great ministers to administer state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Nine great ministers administered the realm.

sentences.zh: 無錢貨，以雜物貿易。

translations.literal: There was no currency; miscellaneous goods were used in trade.
translations.idiomatic: They had no coinage and bartered in kind.

sentences.zh: 其國東行經六月至婆羅門。

translations.literal: Eastward from that state, six months reached Brahmana.
translations.idiomatic: Six months east of his country lay Brahmana.

sentences.zh: 至道二年八月，有天竺僧隨舶至海岸，持帝鍾、鈴杵、銅鈴各一，佛像一軀，貝葉梵書一夾，與之語，不能曉。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the second year of Zhidao, a Tianzhu monk arrived by ship at the coast, holding one imperial bell, one vajra, one bronze bell each, one Buddhist image, and one bundle of palm-leaf Sanskrit books; speaking with him, they could not understand.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the second year of Zhidao an Indian monk arrived by ship at the coast with an imperial bell, a vajra, a bronze bell, a Buddhist image, and a bundle of palm-leaf sutras, but no one could understand his speech.

sentences.zh: 天聖二年九月，西印度僧愛賢、智信護等來獻梵經，各賜紫方袍、束帛。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the second year of Tiansheng, the Western Indian monks Aixian, Zhixinhu, and others came to present Sanskrit scriptures; each was granted a purple square robe and silks.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the second year of Tiansheng the Western Indian monks Aixian, Zhixinhu, and others presented Sanskrit scriptures and each received a purple robe and silks.

sentences.zh: 五年二月，僧法吉祥等五人以梵書來獻，賜紫方袍。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fifth year, the monks Fajixiang and five others came to present Sanskrit books and were granted purple square robes.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the fifth year five monks including Fajixiang presented Sanskrit books and received purple robes.

sentences.zh: 景祐三年正月，僧善稱等九人貢梵經、佛骨及銅牙菩薩像，賜以束帛。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year of Jingyou, the monks Shancheng and nine others presented Sanskrit scriptures, Buddha relics, and a copper-tusked bodhisattva image; they were granted silks.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the third year of Jingyou nine monks including Shancheng presented Sanskrit scriptures, Buddha relics, and a copper bodhisattva image with ivory tusks, and received silks in return.

sentences.zh: 于闐國，自漢至唐，皆入貢中國。

translations.literal: The state of Yutian, from Han through Tang, all entered and presented tribute to China.
translations.idiomatic: Khotan had sent tribute to China from Han through Tang.

sentences.zh: 安、史之亂，絕不復至。

translations.literal: In the rebellion of An and Shi, tribute ceased entirely and did not come again.
translations.idiomatic: After the An Lushan rebellion, the missions ceased entirely.

sentences.zh: 晉天福中，其王李聖天自稱唐之宗屬，遣使來貢。

translations.literal: In the Tianfu era of Jin, its king Li Shengtian called himself a clansman of Tang and sent envoys to present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianfu era of Later Jin its king Li Shengtian claimed descent from the Tang imperial house and sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 高祖命供奉官張匡鄴持節冊聖天為大寶于闐國王。

translations.literal: Gaozu ordered the palace attendant Zhang Kuangye to bear credentials and enfeoff Shengtian as king of Great Treasure Yutian.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu commissioned the palace attendant Zhang Kuangye to invest Shengtian as king of Great Treasure Khotan.

sentences.zh: 建隆二年十二月，聖天遣使貢圭一，以玉為柙；

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the second year of Jianlong, Shengtian sent envoys to present one jade tablet, with jade as its case;
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the second year of Jianlong, Shengtian sent envoys presenting a jade tablet in a jade case;

sentences.zh: 玉枕一。

translations.literal: and one jade pillow.
translations.idiomatic: A jade pillow was also presented.

sentences.zh: 本國摩尼師貢琉璃瓶二、胡錦一段。

translations.literal: The Manichaean master of that land presented two glass bottles and one piece of foreign brocade.
translations.idiomatic: That kingdom's Manichaean master also presented two glass bottles and a length of foreign brocade.

sentences.zh: 其使言：本國去京師九千九百里，西南抵蔥嶺與婆羅門接，相去三千餘里。

translations.literal: Their envoy said: "Our native land is nine thousand nine hundred li from the capital; southwest it reaches Congling and adjoins Brahmana, nine thousand odd li apart."
translations.idiomatic: Their envoy said that Khotan lay nine thousand nine hundred li from the capital, that to the southwest it reached the Pamirs and bordered India three thousand-odd li away.

sentences.zh: 南接吐蕃，西北至疏勒二千餘里。

translations.literal: South it adjoins Tubo; northwest to Shule is more than two thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: To the south it bordered Tibet; northwest to Kashgar was more than two thousand li.

sentences.zh: 國城東有白玉河，西有綠玉河，次西有烏玉河，源出昆岡山，去國城西千三百里。

translations.literal: East of the capital city is the White Jade River, west is the Green Jade River, and next west is the Black Jade River; their source is Mount Kunlun, one thousand three hundred li west of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: East of the capital lay the White Jade River, to the west the Green Jade River, and farther west the Black Jade River, all rising on Mount Kunlun thirteen hundred li west of the city.

sentences.zh: 每歲秋，國人取玉於河，謂之撈玉。

translations.literal: Every autumn the people of the state take jade from the river; this is called "dredging jade."
translations.idiomatic: Each autumn the people dredged jade from the rivers — a practice called "jade-fishing."

sentences.zh: 土宜蒲萄，人多醞以為酒，甚美。

translations.literal: The soil suits grapes; many people ferment them into wine, which is very fine.
translations.idiomatic: The soil favored grapes, and the people made excellent wine from them.

sentences.zh: 俗事妖神。

translations.literal: The custom is to serve demon spirits.
translations.idiomatic: The people worshiped spirits.

sentences.zh: 乾德三年五月，于闐僧善名、善法來朝，賜紫衣。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the third year of Qiande, the Yutian monks Shanming and Shanfa came to court and were granted purple robes.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the third year of Qiande the Khotanese monks Shanming and Shanfa came to court and received purple robes.

sentences.zh: 其國宰相因善名等來，致書樞密使李崇矩，求通中國。

translations.literal: That state's chief minister, because Shanming and others had come, sent a letter to the commissioner of military affairs Li Chongju, seeking communication with China.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom's chief minister, through Shanming and his party, wrote to the military commissioner Li Chongju seeking relations with China.

sentences.zh: 太祖令崇矩以書及器幣報之。

translations.literal: The Taizu Emperor ordered Chongju to reply with a letter and ritual vessels and silks.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu had Chongju reply with a letter, ritual vessels, and silks.

sentences.zh: 至是冬，沙門道圓自西域還，經于闐，與其朝貢使至。

translations.literal: By that winter, the monk Daoyuan returned from the Western Regions, passed through Yutian, and arrived with its tribute embassy.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the monk Daoyuan returned from the west by way of Khotan and arrived with its tribute embassy.

sentences.zh: 四年，又遣其子德從來貢方物。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he again sent his son Decong to present local products.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he sent his son Decong with local products as tribute.

sentences.zh: 開寶二年，遣使直末山來貢，且言本國有玉一塊，凡二百三十七斤，願以上進，乞遣使取之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaibao, he sent the envoy Zhimoshan to present tribute, and added that in his native land there was one block of jade weighing altogether two hundred thirty-seven jin, which he wished to present upward, and asked that envoys be sent to fetch it.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Kaibao he sent the envoy Zhimoshan, reporting a block of jade weighing two hundred thirty-seven jin in his kingdom and asking that envoys be sent to fetch it for presentation.

sentences.zh: 善名復至，貢阿魏子，賜號昭化大師，因令還取玉。

translations.literal: Shanming came again, presenting asafetida seeds; he was granted the title Great Master of Illustrious Transformation, and was thereby ordered to return and fetch the jade.
translations.idiomatic: Shanming came again with asafetida seeds, was granted the title Great Master of Illustrious Transformation, and was sent back to retrieve the jade.

sentences.zh: 又國王男總嘗貢玉欛刀，亦厚賜報之。

translations.literal: Also the king's younger brother Nanzong once presented a jade-handled knife, and he too was richly rewarded in return.
translations.idiomatic: The king's younger brother Nanzong had once presented a knife with a jade handle and likewise received a generous reward.

sentences.zh: 四年，其國僧吉祥以其國王書來上，自言破疏勒國得舞象一，欲以為貢，詔許之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, the monk Jixiang of that state came up with a letter from its king, saying himself that having defeated the state of Shule he obtained one dancing elephant and wished to present it as tribute; an edict permitted this.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year the monk Jixiang presented a letter from his king stating that after defeating Kashgar he had captured a dancing elephant and wished to offer it; the court assented.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符二年，其國黑韓王遣回鶻羅廝溫等以方物來貢。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dazhong Xiangfu, its Black Khan king sent the Uyghur Luosiwen and others with local products to present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Dazhong Xiangfu the Black Khan sent the Uyghur Luosiwen and others with local products as tribute.

sentences.zh: 廝溫跪奏曰：「臣萬里來朝，獲見天日，願聖人萬歲，與遠人作主。」

translations.literal: Siwen knelt and memorialized: "Your subject has come ten thousand li to court, obtained sight of Heaven's sun, and wishes the Sage ten thousand years, to be lord for distant peoples."
translations.idiomatic: Siwen knelt and said: "Your subject has come ten thousand li to court and beheld the light of day; may the Sage live ten thousand years and be lord to distant peoples."

sentences.zh: 上詢以在路幾時，去此幾裏。

translations.literal: The emperor asked how long on the road and how many li from here.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked how long the journey had taken and how far they had traveled.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「涉道一年，晝行暮息，不知里數。

translations.literal: He replied: "We were on the road one year, traveling by day and resting at evening; we do not know the number of li.
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "We were a year on the road, traveling by day and resting at night, and cannot say how many li.

sentences.zh: 昔時道路嘗有剽掠，今自瓜、沙抵于闐，道路清謐，行旅如流。

translations.literal: Formerly the roads often had plunder; now from Guazhou and Shazhou to Yutian the roads are tranquil and travelers flow like a stream.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits once plagued the route, but now from Guazhou and Shazhou to Khotan the road is peaceful and travelers pass in steady streams.

sentences.zh: 願遣使安撫遠俗。」

translations.literal: We wish that envoys be sent to pacify distant customs."
translations.idiomatic: We beg that envoys be sent to reassure the distant peoples."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「路遠命使，益以勞費爾國。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The road is far; ordering envoys would only add to the labor and expense of your state.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "The distance is great; to send envoys would only burden your kingdom further.

sentences.zh: 今降詔書，汝即齎往，亦與命使無異也。」

translations.literal: Now I issue an edict; you may carry it back at once — this is no different from sending envoys."
translations.idiomatic: I shall issue an edict for you to carry home — that will serve the same purpose as envoys."

sentences.zh: 初，太平興國中有澶州卒王貴者，晝忽見使者至營，急召貴偕行，南至河橋，驛馬已具，即命乘之，俄覺騰虛而去。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the Taiping Xingguo era there was a Tanzhou soldier named Wang Gui; in daylight he suddenly saw envoys arrive at the camp, urgently summoning Gui to go with them; south to the river bridge, relay horses were already prepared, and he was ordered to mount; presently he felt himself soaring through the void and departing.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in the Taiping Xingguo era, a Tanzhou soldier named Wang Gui was suddenly summoned in broad daylight by envoys who hurried him south to the river bridge, where relay horses waited. He mounted and felt himself lifted into the air.

sentences.zh: 頃之駐馬，但見屋室宏麗，使者引貴入，見其主者容衛制度悉如王者。

translations.literal: Shortly he halted his horse and saw only grand and splendid halls; the envoys led Gui in, and he saw that the lord's appearance, guards, and institutions were all like a king's.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he dismounted before magnificent halls. The envoys led him in to a lord whose guards and court ceremonial were those of a king.

sentences.zh: 謂貴曰：「俟汝年五十八，當往于闐國北通聖山取一異寶以奉皇帝，宜深誌之。」

translations.literal: He said to Gui: "When you reach fifty-eight years of age, you shall go to the Sacred Communication Mountain north of Yutian to fetch a wondrous treasure to present to the emperor; you should deeply remember this."
translations.idiomatic: The lord told him: "When you are fifty-eight, go to the Sacred Communication Mountain north of Khotan and fetch a wondrous treasure for the emperor. Keep this deeply in mind."

sentences.zh: 遂復乘馬淩虛而旋。

translations.literal: Then he again mounted his horse and returned through the void.
translations.idiomatic: Then he mounted again and was borne back through the air.

sentences.zh: 軍中失貴已數日矣，驗所乘，即營卒之馬也。

translations.literal: The army had lost Gui for several days already; examining the mount he rode, it was the camp soldier's horse.
translations.idiomatic: The camp had missed him for days; the horse he rode was his own from the garrison.

sentences.zh: 知州宋煦劾貴以聞，太宗釋之。

translations.literal: The prefect Song Xu impeached Gui and reported upward; Taizong released him.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Song Xu reported the matter; Taizong pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 天禧初，貴自陳年已五十八，願遵前戒，西至于闐，尋許其行。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianxi, Gui stated himself that he was already fifty-eight and wished to follow the former command, going west to Yutian; soon his journey was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianxi, Gui declared that he was fifty-eight and asked leave to fulfill the command by traveling west to Khotan; permission was granted.

sentences.zh: 貴至秦州，以道遠悔懼，俄於市中遇一道士引貴出城，登高原，問貴所欲，具以實對。

translations.literal: Gui reached Qinzhou; because the road was far he regretted and feared; presently in the market he met a Daoist who led Gui out of the city, climbed a high plateau, and asked what Gui desired; he answered fully with the truth.
translations.idiomatic: At Qinzhou, daunted by the distance, he met a Daoist in the market who led him outside the city to a high plateau and asked his purpose; Gui told him everything.

sentences.zh: 即命貴閉目，少頃令開，視山川頓異，道士曰：「此于闐國北境通聖山也。」

translations.literal: He then ordered Gui to close his eyes; after a moment he told him to open them — the mountains and rivers were suddenly different. The Daoist said: "This is the Sacred Communication Mountain on the northern border of Yutian."
translations.idiomatic: The Daoist bade him close his eyes; when he opened them the landscape had changed utterly. The Daoist said: "This is the Sacred Communication Mountain on Khotan's northern frontier."

sentences.zh: 復引貴觀一池，池中有仙童，出一物授之，謂曰：「持此奉皇帝。」

translations.literal: He again led Gui to view a pool; in the pool was an immortal youth, who brought out one object and handed it to him, saying: "Take this to present to the emperor."
translations.idiomatic: He led him to a pool where an immortal youth handed him an object, saying: "Take this to the emperor."

sentences.zh: 又令瞑目，俄頃復至秦州，向之道士已失所在，發其物乃玉印也，文曰「國王趙萬永寶」，州以獻。

translations.literal: He again ordered him to close his eyes; in a moment he was back at Qinzhou; the former Daoist was already gone; opening the object, it was a jade seal; the inscription read "Treasure of King Zhao Wan of the State"; the prefecture presented it upward.
translations.idiomatic: He closed his eyes again and was suddenly back at Qinzhou; the Daoist had vanished. The object proved to be a jade seal inscribed "Treasure of King Zhao Wan of the State," which the prefecture presented to the throne.

sentences.zh: 天聖三年十二月，遣使羅麵於多、副使金三、監使安多、都監趙多來朝，貢玉鞍轡、白玉帶、胡錦、獨峰橐駝、乳香、硇砂。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the third year of Tiansheng, envoys were sent — Luomianyuduo as chief, Jin San as vice, Anduo as supervisor, Zhao Duo as chief inspector — who came to court, presenting jade saddle and bridle, white jade belt, foreign brocade, single-hump Bactrian camels, frankincense, and sal ammoniac.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the third year of Tiansheng envoys led by Luomianyuduo, with Jin San as vice-envoy, Anduo as supervisor, and Zhao Duo as chief inspector, came to court with jade saddle and bridle, a white jade belt, foreign brocade, Bactrian camels, frankincense, and sal ammoniac.

sentences.zh: 詔給還其直，館於都亭西驛，別賜襲衣、金帶、銀器百兩、衣著二百，羅麵於多金帶。

translations.literal: An edict ordered their compensation paid back, lodged them at the Duting West Post Station, and separately bestowed formal robes, gold belts, one hundred liang of silver vessels, two hundred sets of garments, and a gold belt for Luomianyuduo.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered payment for their tribute restored and had them lodged at the Duting West Post Station, with additional gifts of court robes, gold belts, silverware weighing one hundred liang, two hundred sets of clothing, and a gold belt for Luomianyuduo.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐八年八月，遣使羅撒溫獻方物。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the eighth year of Jiayou, envoys led by Luosawen presented local products.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the eighth year of Jiayou, an embassy led by Luosawen brought tribute goods.

sentences.zh: 十一月，以其國王為特進、歸忠保順後鱗黑韓王。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, their king was made Special Advancement, King of Gui-Zhong-Bao-Shun Houlin Black Khan — the garbled Houlin element standing in for a golden-winged-bird title.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month their king was enfeoffed as Special Advancement, Loyal and Fidelity-Preserving Houlin Black Khan King.

sentences.zh: 羅撒溫言其王乞賜此號也，于闐謂金翅烏為「後鱗」，「黑韓」蓋可汗之訛也。

translations.literal: Luosawen said their king had begged to be granted this title; in Khotan the golden-winged bird is called "Houlin," and "Black Han" is probably a corruption of "khan."
translations.idiomatic: Luosawen explained that their king had requested this title: in Khotan the golden-winged bird is called "Houlin," and "Black Han" is likely a mispronunciation of khan.

sentences.zh: 羅撒溫等以獻物賜直少不受，及請所獻獨峰橐駝。

translations.literal: Luosawen and the others, because the compensation for their tribute goods was too little, would not accept it, and also requested the single-hump Bactrian camel they had presented.
translations.idiomatic: Luosawen and his party refused the compensation offered for their tribute as insufficient and asked that the single-hump Bactrian camel they had presented be returned.

sentences.zh: 詔以遠人特別賜錢五千貫，以橐駝還之，而與其已賜之直。

translations.literal: An edict specially granted these distant envoys five thousand strings of cash, returned the camel to them, and also gave them the compensation already bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: An edict specially granted the distant envoys five thousand strings of cash, returned their camel, and paid them the compensation already awarded.

sentences.zh: 其後數以方物來獻。

translations.literal: Afterward they came repeatedly with local products as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter they sent tribute missions on many occasions.

sentences.zh: 熙寧以來，遠不逾一二歲，近則歲再至。

translations.literal: Since Xining, when the distance was great it was no more than one or two years between visits; when near, they came twice a year.
translations.idiomatic: From the Xining era onward, when the journey was long they came at most every year or two; when nearer at hand they came twice a year.

sentences.zh: 所貢珠玉、珊瑚、翡翠、象牙、乳香、木香、琥珀、花蕊布、硇砂、龍鹽、西錦、玉秋轡馬、膃肭臍、金星石、水銀、安息雞舌香，有所持無表章，每賜以暈錦旋襴衣、金帶、器幣，宰相則盤球雲錦夾襴。

translations.literal: They offered pearls and jade, coral, kingfisher feathers, ivory, frankincense, aloeswood, amber, flower-stamen cloth, sal ammoniac, dragon salt, western brocade, horses with jade autumn bridles, musk pods, golden-star stone, mercury, and styrax from Parthia; some carried goods without memorials, yet each was bestowed halo-brocade spiral-hem robes, gold belts, and ritual vessels — grand councilors received panqiu cloud-brocade lined robes.
translations.idiomatic: Their tribute included pearls and jade, coral, kingfisher feathers, ivory, frankincense, aloeswood, amber, flower-stamen cloth, sal ammoniac, dragon salt, western brocade, jade-bridled horses, musk pods, golden-star stone, mercury, and Parthian styrax. Even when envoys brought goods but no memorial, each was rewarded with halo-brocade spiral-hem robes, gold belts, and ritual gifts; grand councilors received panqiu cloud-brocade lined robes.

sentences.zh: 地產乳香，來輒群負，私與商賈牟利；

translations.literal: The land produced frankincense; when they came they always carried it in groups on their backs and privately traded with merchants for profit.
translations.idiomatic: Because frankincense was native to their country, envoys arrived in groups laden with it and traded privately with merchants for profit.

sentences.zh: 不售，則歸諸外府得善價，故其來益多。

translations.literal: If it did not sell, they turned it over to the outer prefectures and obtained a good price, so their coming grew ever more frequent.
translations.idiomatic: What they could not sell they sold on through frontier prefectures at favorable prices, so their missions became ever more numerous.

sentences.zh: 元豐初，始詔惟齎表及方物馬驢乃聽以詣闕，乳香無用不許貢。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanfeng, an edict first ruled that only those bearing memorials together with local products, horses, and donkeys would be permitted to proceed to court; useless frankincense was not allowed as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Yuanfeng an edict stipulated that only envoys carrying memorials together with tribute goods, horses, or donkeys might proceed to court; frankincense alone was barred from tribute.

sentences.zh: 四年，遣部領阿辛上表稱「于闐國僂羅有福力量知文法黑汗王，書與東方日出處大世界田地主漢家阿舅大官家」，大略雲路遠傾心相向，前三遣使入貢未回，重復數百言。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, the envoy leader Axin submitted a memorial stating, "The King of Khotan, Uluo Youfu, possessor of strength and knowledge of the law, Black Khan, writes to the great Han official family, maternal uncle to the lord of the great world where the sun rises in the east over the fields," roughly saying that though the road was far their hearts inclined toward the court; the three previous embassies sent with tribute had not returned — several hundred words repeated.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year envoy leader Axin submitted a memorial in the name of "Uluo Youfu, King of Khotan, possessor of strength and versed in the law, Black Khan," addressed to "the great Han official family, maternal uncle to the lord of the great world where the sun rises in the east." It declared that though the road was long their hearts turned toward the court, lamented that three earlier tribute missions had not returned, and ran to several hundred words.

sentences.zh: 董氈使導至熙州，譯其辭以聞。

translations.literal: Dongzhan's envoys guided them to Xizhou, and their words were translated and reported upward.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys of Dongzhan escorted them to Xizhou, where the memorial was translated and reported to the throne.

sentences.zh: 詔前三輩使人皆已朝見，錫賚遣發，賜敕書諭之。

translations.literal: An edict stated that the envoys of the three previous missions had all already been received in audience, rewarded, and sent on their way, and an imperial letter of instruction was bestowed to inform them.
translations.idiomatic: An edict explained that the three earlier embassies had all been received, rewarded, and dismissed, and an imperial letter was sent to reassure them.

sentences.zh: 神宗嘗問其使去國歲月，所經何國及有無鈔略。

translations.literal: Shenzong once asked their envoys how many months and years they had been away from their country, what states they had passed through, and whether there had been any plundering.
translations.idiomatic: Shenzong once asked the envoys how long they had been away from home, which countries they had passed through, and whether they had suffered any raids.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「去國四年，道塗居其半，歷黃頭回紇、青唐，惟懼契丹鈔略耳。」

translations.literal: They replied: "We have been four years from our country; the road took half of that. We passed through the Yellow-Head Uyghurs and Qingtang, and feared only plunder by the Khitan."
translations.idiomatic: They answered: "We have been four years from home, half of that spent on the road. We passed through the Yellow-Head Uyghurs and Qingtang and feared only Khitan raids."

sentences.zh: 因使之圖上諸國距漢境遠近，為書以授李憲。

translations.literal: Accordingly they were made to map the various states and their distances from the Han frontier, and a written account was prepared and given to Li Xian.
translations.idiomatic: They were then told to chart the various states and their distances from the Song frontier, and a written report was prepared for Li Xian.

sentences.zh: 八年九月，遣使入貢，使者為神宗飯僧追福。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the eighth year, envoys came with tribute; the envoys were feeding monks on Shenzong's behalf to seek merit for his soul.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the eighth year envoys arrived with tribute; they had come to feed monks and accrue merit on Shenzong's behalf.

sentences.zh: 賜錢百萬，還其所貢師子。

translations.literal: They were granted one million cash and their presented lion was returned.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted them one million cash and returned the lion they had presented.

sentences.zh: 元祐中，以其使至無時，令熙河間歲一聽至闕。

translations.literal: During Yuanyou, because their envoys arrived at no fixed time, the Xihe region was ordered to permit one mission a year to proceed to court.
translations.idiomatic: During Yuanyou, since Khotanese envoys arrived irregularly, the court allowed one mission per year from the Xihe region to proceed to court.

sentences.zh: 八年，請討夏國，不許。

translations.literal: In the eighth year they requested permission to attack the Xia state; it was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year they asked leave to campaign against Western Xia; the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 紹聖中，其王阿忽都董娥密竭篤又言，緬藥家作過，別無報效，已遣兵攻甘、沙、肅三州。

translations.literal: During Shaosheng, their king Ahudu Dong'emijiedu again reported that the Mianyao clan had rebelled and that, having no other way to repay the court's favor, he had already sent troops to attack the three prefectures of Gan, Sha, and Su.
translations.idiomatic: During Shaosheng King Ahudu Dong'emijiedu reported that the Mianyao clan had risen in rebellion and that, lacking other means to repay the court, he had already dispatched troops against Gan, Sha, and Su prefectures.

sentences.zh: 詔厚答其意。

translations.literal: An edict warmly responded to his intent.
translations.idiomatic: An edict warmly acknowledged his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 知秦州遊師雄言：「于闐、大食、拂菻等國貢奉，般次踵至，有司憚於供賚，抑留邊方，限二歲一進。

translations.literal: You Shixiong, prefect of Qinzhou, said: "Tribute missions from Khotan, Dashi, Fulin, and other states arrive one after another in succession; the officials, fearing the cost of entertaining them, detain them on the frontier and limit them to one visit every two years.
translations.idiomatic: Qinzhou prefect You Shixiong said: "Tribute missions from Khotan, the Arabs, Byzantium, and other lands arrive in an unbroken stream. Local officials, daunted by the cost of receiving them, hold them on the frontier and restrict them to one visit every two years.

sentences.zh: 外夷慕義，萬里而至，此非所以來遠人也。」

translations.literal: Foreign peoples who admire righteousness come ten thousand li — this is not the way to draw distant peoples.
translations.idiomatic: Peoples from afar who admire our virtue travel ten thousand li to reach us — this is no way to win distant peoples."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The court assented.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 自是訖於宣和，朝享不絕。

translations.literal: From then until Xuanhe, court audiences never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: From then until the Xuanhe era, tribute audiences continued without interruption.

sentences.zh: 高昌國，漢車師前王之地。

translations.literal: The state of Gaochang was the land of the Former King of Cheshi in Han times.
translations.idiomatic: Gaochang occupied the territory of the Former King of Cheshi in Han times.

sentences.zh: 有高昌城，取其地勢高敞、人民昌盛以為名焉。

translations.literal: There was Gaochang city, named for its lofty, open terrain and flourishing population.
translations.idiomatic: Its capital was Gaochang city, named for the lofty openness of the land and the prosperity of its people.

sentences.zh: 後魏初，沮渠無諱自署高昌太守。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Later Wei, Juqu Wuhui styled himself Prefect of Gaochang.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Northern Wei, Juqu Wuhui declared himself prefect of Gaochang.

sentences.zh: 無諱死，茹茹以闞伯周為高昌王，高昌有王始於此。

translations.literal: When Wuhui died, the Ruru installed Kan Bozhou as King of Gaochang — from this Gaochang first had a king.
translations.idiomatic: After Wuhui's death the Rouran installed Kan Bozhou as king of Gaochang, and Gaochang first acquired a royal line at that point.

sentences.zh: 後魏至隋皆來貢獻。

translations.literal: From Later Wei through Sui they all came with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: From the Northern Wei through the Sui dynasty they sent tribute missions.

sentences.zh: 唐貞觀中，侯君集平其國，以其地為西州。

translations.literal: In the Zhenguan era of Tang, Hou Junji pacified their state and made their land Xizhou.
translations.idiomatic: During Tang Zhenguan, Hou Junji conquered the kingdom and reorganized its territory as Xizhou.

sentences.zh: 安、史之亂，其地陷沒，乃復為國。

translations.literal: In the rebellion of An and Shi their land was lost, and it again became an independent state.
translations.idiomatic: After the An Lushan–Shi Siming rebellion the region fell away from Tang control and became a kingdom once more.

sentences.zh: 語訛亦云「高敞」，然其地頗有回鶻，故亦謂之回鶻。

translations.literal: In corrupted speech it was also called "Gaochang" in the sense of "high and open," yet because there were many Uyghurs in the land it was also called Uyghur.
translations.idiomatic: Local pronunciation also rendered the name as "high and open," but because many Uyghurs lived there it was also known as Uyghur.

sentences.zh: 建隆三年四月，西州回鶻阿都督等四十二人以方物來貢。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the third year of Jianlong, forty-two men including Commander A of Xizhou Uyghur came with local products as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the third year of Jianlong, forty-two Xizhou Uyghurs led by Commander A brought tribute goods.

sentences.zh: 乾德三年十一月，西州回鶻可汗遣僧法淵獻佛牙、琉璃器、琥珀盞。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the third year of Qiande, the khan of Xizhou Uyghur sent the monk Fayuan to present a Buddha tooth, glass vessels, and an amber cup.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the third year of Qiande the khan of Xizhou Uyghur sent the monk Fayuan with a Buddha tooth, glassware, and an amber goblet.

sentences.zh: 太平興國六年，其王始稱西州外生師子王阿廝蘭漢，遣都督麥索溫來獻。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Taiping Xingguo, their king first styled himself Lion King Asilanhan, maternal nephew of Xizhou, and sent Commander Maisuowen to present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Taiping Xingguo their king first took the title Lion King Asilanhan, maternal nephew of Xizhou, and sent Commander Maisuowen with tribute.

sentences.zh: 五月，太宗遣供奉官王延德、殿前承旨白勳使高昌。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Taizong dispatched Palace Attendant Wang Yande and Palace Front Commissioner Bai Xun as envoys to Gaochang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Taizong sent Palace Attendant Wang Yande and Palace Front Commissioner Bai Xun as envoys to Gaochang.

sentences.zh: 八年，其使安鶻盧來貢。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, their envoy Anhelu came with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year their envoy Anhelu arrived with tribute.

sentences.zh: 雍熙元年四月，王延德等還，敘其行程來獻，云：

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the first year of Yongxi, Wang Yande and the others returned, narrated their itinerary, and presented it as tribute, saying:
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the first year of Yongxi Wang Yande and his party returned, submitted an account of their journey, and reported:

sentences.zh: 初自夏州曆玉亭鎮，次曆黃羊平，其地平而產黃羊。

translations.literal: At first they set out from Xiazhou and passed through Yuting Post; next they passed through Yellow Sheep Plain, which was level and produced yellow sheep.
translations.idiomatic: They set out from Xiazhou and passed through Yuting Post, then Yellow Sheep Plain — level country where yellow sheep grazed.

sentences.zh: 渡沙磧，無水，行人皆載水。

translations.literal: Crossing sandy desert, there was no water; travelers all carried water.
translations.idiomatic: Crossing the sandy desert, where there was no water, every traveler carried his own supply.

sentences.zh: 凡二日至都囉囉族，漢使過者，遺以財貨，謂之「打當」。

translations.literal: In all two days to the Duluo tribe; when Han envoys passed through, gifts of goods were left — this was called "da dang."
translations.idiomatic: After two days they reached the Duluo tribe, where Han envoys passing through left gifts of goods in a custom called "da dang."

sentences.zh: 次曆茅女子族，族臨黃河，以羊皮為囊，吹氣實之浮於水，或以橐駝牽木栰而渡。

translations.literal: Next they passed through the Mao-nüzi tribe, which bordered the Yellow River; they made bags of sheepskin, inflated them to float on the water, or had Bactrian camels pull wooden rafts to cross.
translations.idiomatic: Next came the Mao-nüzi tribe on the Yellow River, where people crossed by inflating sheepskin floats or by having camels tow wooden rafts.

sentences.zh: 次曆茅女王子開道族，行入六窠沙，沙深三尺，馬不能行，行者皆乘橐駝。

translations.literal: Next they passed through the Mao-nü Prince Kaidao tribe; entering the Six-Nest Sands, the sand was three feet deep and horses could not travel — travelers all rode Bactrian camels.
translations.idiomatic: They then passed the Mao-nü Prince Kaidao tribe and entered the Six-Nest Sands, where the sand lay three feet deep, horses could not pass, and everyone rode camels.

sentences.zh: 不育五穀，沙中生草名登相，收之以食。

translations.literal: They did not cultivate the five grains; in the sand grew a grass called dengxiang, which they gathered for food.
translations.idiomatic: They grew no grain; instead they gathered a desert grass called dengxiang for food.

sentences.zh: 次曆樓子山，無居人。

translations.literal: Next they passed Mount Louzi; there were no inhabitants.
translations.idiomatic: They next crossed Mount Louzi, uninhabited country.

sentences.zh: 行沙磧中，以日為占，旦則背日，暮則向日，日中則止。

translations.literal: Traveling in the sandy desert, they took the sun as their guide: at dawn they went with their backs to the sun, at dusk they faced the sun, and at midday they halted.
translations.idiomatic: Crossing the desert they navigated by the sun — marching with their backs to it at dawn, facing it at dusk, and resting at noon.

sentences.zh: 夕行望月亦如之。

translations.literal: Traveling at night they took the moon in the same way.
translations.idiomatic: When they traveled at night they steered by the moon in the same fashion.

sentences.zh: 次曆臥梁劾特族地，有都督山，唐回鶻之地。

translations.literal: Next they passed the land of the Wolianhete tribe; there was Commander Mountain — Tang Uyghur territory.
translations.idiomatic: They next crossed the land of the Wolianhete tribe, where Commander Mountain marked old Tang Uyghur territory.

sentences.zh: 次曆大蟲太子族，族接契丹界，人衣尚錦繡，器用金銀，馬乳釀酒，飲之亦醉。

translations.literal: Next they passed the Great Tiger Prince tribe, which bordered Khitan territory; the people favored brocade and embroidery in dress, used gold and silver for vessels, fermented wine from mare's milk, and became drunk drinking it.
translations.idiomatic: They then reached the Great Tiger Prince tribe on the Khitan frontier, where people wore brocade and embroidery, used gold and silver vessels, and drank fermented mare's milk until drunk.

sentences.zh: 次曆屋地因族，蓋達於於越王子之子。

translations.literal: Next they passed the Wudiyin tribe — descendants of the son of Dayu Yuyuezi.
translations.idiomatic: Next came the Wudiyin tribe, said to be descended from the son of Prince Dayu Yuyue.

sentences.zh: 次至達於於越王子族。

translations.literal: Next they reached the Dayu Yuyuezi tribe.
translations.idiomatic: They then arrived at the Dayu Yuyuezi tribe.

sentences.zh: 次曆拽利王子族，有合羅川，唐回鶻公主所居之地，城基尚在，有湯泉池。

translations.literal: Next they passed the Prince Zhuaili tribe; there was Heluo River, where the Tang Uyghur princess had dwelt — city foundations still remained, and there were hot-spring pools.
translations.idiomatic: They next passed the Prince Zhuaili tribe, where Heluo River marked the former seat of a Tang Uyghur princess; city foundations still stood and hot springs bubbled nearby.

sentences.zh: 次曆阿墩族，經馬鬃山望鄉嶺，嶺上石龕有李陵題字處。

translations.literal: Next they passed the Adun tribe, crossed Mane Mountain and Wangxiang Ridge; on the ridge in a stone niche was the place where Li Ling had inscribed characters.
translations.idiomatic: They next crossed the Adun tribe's territory, passing Mane Mountain and Wangxiang Ridge, where a stone niche bore an inscription said to be Li Ling's.

sentences.zh: 次曆格囉美源，西方百川所會，極望無際，鷗鷺鳧雁之類甚眾。

translations.literal: Next they passed Gelamei Spring, where the hundred streams of the west converged; gazing to the limit there was no end, and gulls, egrets, ducks, and wild geese were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: They next reached Gelamei Spring, where western rivers converged in a vista without horizon, teeming with gulls, egrets, ducks, and wild geese.

sentences.zh: 次至托邊城，亦名李僕射城，城中首領號「通天王」。

translations.literal: Next they reached Tuobian city, also called Vice Censor-in-Chief Li's city; the chief in the city was styled "Heaven-Penetrating King."
translations.idiomatic: They next reached Tuobian city, also known as Vice Censor Li's city, whose local ruler styled himself "Heaven-Penetrating King."

sentences.zh: 次曆小石州。

translations.literal: Next they passed Little Shizhou.
translations.idiomatic: They next passed through Little Shizhou.

sentences.zh: 次曆伊州，州將陳氏，其先自唐開元二年領州，凡數十世，唐時詔敕尚在。

translations.literal: Next they passed Yizhou; the prefect was of the Chen clan, whose ancestors had held the prefecture since the second year of Tang Kaiyuan — for several tens of generations — and Tang edicts and orders were still preserved.
translations.idiomatic: They next reached Yizhou, governed for dozens of generations by the Chen family since Tang Kaiyuan 2; imperial Tang edicts were still kept there.

sentences.zh: 地有野蠶生苦參上，可為綿帛。

translations.literal: In the land wild silkworms grew on sophora, from which cotton and silk cloth could be made.
translations.idiomatic: Wild silkworms fed on sophora there, yielding thread for cotton and silk cloth.

sentences.zh: 有羊，尾大而不能走，尾重者三斤，小者一斤，肉如熊白而甚美。

translations.literal: There were sheep with large tails that could not run; the heavy tails weighed three jin, the small ones one jin, and the flesh was like bear's paw and very delicious.
translations.idiomatic: Sheep there had tails so large and heavy — up to three jin — that the animals could barely walk; the meat was tender as bear's paw and exceedingly fine.

sentences.zh: 又有礪石，剖之得賓鐵，謂之吃鐵石。

translations.literal: There was also whetstone; split open it yielded fine iron — called iron-eating stone.
translations.idiomatic: Whetstones found there, when split, yielded fine iron in what they called iron-eating stone.

sentences.zh: 又生胡桐樹，經雨即生胡桐律。

translations.literal: Tamarisk trees also grew there; after rain they produced tamarisk cones.
translations.idiomatic: Tamarisk trees grew there as well; after rain they sprouted tamarisk cones.

sentences.zh: 次曆益都。

translations.literal: Next they passed Yidu.
translations.idiomatic: They next passed Yidu.

sentences.zh: 次曆納職城，城在大患鬼魅磧之東南，望玉門關甚近。

translations.literal: Next they passed Nazhi city; the city lay southeast of the Great Peril Ghost-Demon Desert, and from it one could see Yumen Pass very near.
translations.idiomatic: They next reached Nazhi city southeast of the Great Peril Ghost-Demon Desert, from which Yumen Pass seemed close at hand.

sentences.zh: 地無水草，載糧以行。

translations.literal: The land had no water or grass; they carried provisions to travel.
translations.idiomatic: The country offered no water or pasture, so they carried grain for the march.

sentences.zh: 凡三日，至鬼穀口避風驛，用本國法設祭，出詔神御風，風乃息。

translations.literal: In all three days they reached the Wind-Shelter Post at Ghost Valley Mouth; using their own country's rites they set out offerings, issued a proclamation to the spirit to control the wind, and the wind then ceased.
translations.idiomatic: After three days they reached the Wind-Shelter Post at Ghost Valley Mouth, performed rites by their own customs, invoked the spirit to still the wind, and the gale subsided.

sentences.zh: 凡八日，至澤田寺。

translations.literal: In all eight days they reached Zetian Monastery.
translations.idiomatic: Eight days later they reached Zetian Monastery.

sentences.zh: 高昌聞使至，遣人來迎。

translations.literal: Gaochang, hearing that envoys had arrived, sent people to welcome them.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that the envoys had arrived, Gaochang sent men to meet them.

sentences.zh: 次歷地名寶莊，又歷六種，乃至高昌。

translations.literal: Next they passed a place called Baozhuang, then passed six more tribes, and thus reached Gaochang.
translations.idiomatic: They next passed a place called Baozhuang, crossed six more tribal territories, and at last arrived at Gaochang.

sentences.zh: 高昌即西州也。

translations.literal: Gaochang was Xizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gaochang was the same as Xizhou.

sentences.zh: 其地南距于闐，西南距大食、波斯，西距西天步路涉、雪山、蔥嶺，皆數千里。

translations.literal: Its land was several thousand li south from Khotan, southwest from Dashi and Persia, and west from the roads of the Western Heaven, Bushlushe, Snow Mountains, and Congling — all several thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: It lay several thousand li south of Khotan, southwest of the Arabs and Persia, and west of the routes to India, Bushlushe, the Snow Mountains, and the Pamirs.

sentences.zh: 地無雨雪而極熱，每盛暑，居人皆穿地為穴以處。

translations.literal: The land had no rain or snow but was extremely hot; in every midsummer the inhabitants all dug into the earth for caves to dwell in.
translations.idiomatic: Rain and snow never fell there, yet the heat was extreme; in high summer people lived in underground chambers dug from the earth.

sentences.zh: 飛鳥群萃河濱，或起飛，即為日氣所爍，墜而傷翼。

translations.literal: Birds gathered in flocks along the river; when they rose to fly they were scorched by the sun's heat, fell, and injured their wings.
translations.idiomatic: Birds flocked along the rivers; when they took flight the sun's heat scorched them and they fell with broken wings.

sentences.zh: 屋室覆以白堊，雨及五寸，即廬舍多壞。

translations.literal: Houses were roofed with white plaster; when rain reached five inches many dwellings were ruined.
translations.idiomatic: Houses were whitewashed, yet when as little as five inches of rain fell many dwellings collapsed.

sentences.zh: 有水，源出金嶺，導之周圍國城，以溉田園，作水磑。

translations.literal: There was water whose source issued from Golden Ridge; it was channeled around the state and city to irrigate fields and gardens and to drive water mills.
translations.idiomatic: Water from Golden Ridge was channeled around the kingdom to irrigate fields and gardens and to power water mills.

sentences.zh: 地產五穀，惟無蕎麥。

translations.literal: The land produced the five grains, only lacking buckwheat.
translations.idiomatic: All five grains grew there except buckwheat.

sentences.zh: 貴人食馬，餘食羊及鳧雁。

translations.literal: Nobles ate horse; the rest ate sheep and ducks and wild geese.
translations.idiomatic: The nobility ate horseflesh; others ate mutton, duck, and wild goose.

sentences.zh: 樂多琵琶、箜篌。

translations.literal: In music there were mostly pipa and konghou.
translations.idiomatic: Their music favored the pipa and konghou.

sentences.zh: 出貂鼠、白氎、繡文花蕊布。

translations.literal: They produced sable, white felt, and embroidered flower-stamen cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Local products included sable, white felt, and embroidered flower-stamen cloth.

sentences.zh: 俗好騎射。

translations.literal: Their custom favored mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: They were fond of mounted archery.

sentences.zh: 婦人戴油帽，謂之蘇幕遮。

translations.literal: Women wore oiled hats — called sumuzhe.
translations.idiomatic: Women wore oiled hats in a style called sumuzhe.

sentences.zh: 用開元七年曆，以三月九日為寒食，餘二社、冬至亦然。

translations.literal: They used the calendar of the seventh year of Kaiyuan, taking the ninth day of the third month as Cold Food Festival; the two She festivals and the winter solstice were the same.
translations.idiomatic: They followed the Kaiyuan 7 calendar, observing Cold Food on the ninth day of the third month and fixing the two She festivals and the winter solstice by the same reckoning.

sentences.zh: 以銀或鍮石為筒，貯水激以相射，或以水交潑為戲，謂之壓陽氣去病。

translations.literal: They made tubes of silver or brass, stored water, and squirted it at one another, or splashed water on each other in play — called suppressing yang qi to drive away illness.
translations.idiomatic: They fashioned tubes of silver or brass, filled them with water, and squirted or splashed one another in a rite said to suppress excess yang and ward off disease.

sentences.zh: 好游賞，行者必抱樂器。

translations.literal: They loved outings; travelers always carried musical instruments.
translations.idiomatic: They loved outings and never traveled without musical instruments.

sentences.zh: 佛寺五十餘區，皆唐朝所賜額，寺中有《大藏經》、《唐韻》、《玉篇》、《經音》等，居民春月多群聚遨樂於其間。

translations.literal: There were more than fifty Buddhist monasteries, all granted plaques by Tang; in the monasteries were the Great Canon, Tangyun, Yupian, Jingyin, and the like, and in spring the residents often gathered in groups for merrymaking among them.
translations.idiomatic: More than fifty Buddhist monasteries bore Tang-donated name plaques and housed the Great Canon, Tangyun, Yupian, Jingyin, and similar works; in spring people gathered there in festive groups.

sentences.zh: 遊者馬上持弓矢射諸物，謂之禳災。

translations.literal: Outing-goers on horseback held bows and arrows and shot at various objects — called dispelling calamity.
translations.idiomatic: On outings riders shot at targets from horseback in a rite called dispelling calamity.

sentences.zh: 有敕書樓，藏唐太宗、明皇御劄詔敕，緘鎖甚謹。

translations.literal: There was an Edict Archive Tower storing imperial letters and edicts of Tang Taizong and Minghuang, sealed and locked with great care.
translations.idiomatic: An Edict Archive Tower held sealed imperial letters and edicts of Tang Taizong and Emperor Xuanzong, guarded with great care.

sentences.zh: 復有摩尼寺，波斯僧各持其法，佛經所謂外道者也。

translations.literal: There were also Manichaean temples; Persian monks each upheld their own law — what Buddhist scriptures call heterodox paths.
translations.idiomatic: Manichaean temples stood there as well, where Persian monks practiced their own faith — the "heterodox paths" of Buddhist scripture.

sentences.zh: 所統有南突厥、北突厥、大眾熨、小眾熨、樣磨、割祿、黠戛司、末蠻、格哆族、預龍族之名甚眾。

translations.literal: Under their rule were very many names: Southern Turk, Northern Turk, Great Zhongyi, Little Zhongyi, Yangmo, Gelu, Xiajiasi, Moman, Geduo tribe, Yulong tribe, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: They ruled over a great many peoples, including the Southern and Northern Turks, the Great and Little Zhongyi, Yangmo, Gelu, Xiajiasi, Moman, the Geduo tribe, the Yulong tribe, and many others.

sentences.zh: 國中無貧民，絕食者共賑之。

translations.literal: In the state there were no poor people; those without food were jointly relieved.
translations.idiomatic: There were no destitute people in the kingdom; anyone without food was supported by communal relief.

sentences.zh: 人多壽考，率百餘歲，絕地夭死。

translations.literal: People mostly lived long; on average over a hundred years, and premature death was utterly absent.
translations.idiomatic: People commonly lived to ripe old age, often past a hundred, and early death was virtually unknown.

sentences.zh: 時四月，師子王避暑於北廷，以其舅阿多於越守國，先遣人致意於延德曰：「我王舅也，使者拜我乎？」

translations.literal: It was the fourth month; the Lion King was summering at Beiting and had left his maternal uncle Aduoyuyue to guard the state. He first sent someone to convey his intent to Yande, saying: "I am the king's maternal uncle — will the envoy bow to me?"
translations.idiomatic: It was the fourth month; the Lion King was summering at Beiting and had left his maternal uncle Aduoyuyue to govern the realm. Aduoyuyue sent word ahead to Yande: "I am the king's uncle — will you bow to me?"

sentences.zh: 延德曰：「持朝命而來，禮不當拜。」

translations.literal: Yande said: "Coming bearing the court's command, by ritual one should not bow."
translations.idiomatic: Yande replied: "I come bearing the court's commission; protocol does not require a bow."

sentences.zh: 復問曰：「見王拜乎？」

translations.literal: He asked again: "When you meet the king, will you bow?"
translations.idiomatic: He asked again: "Will you bow when you meet the king?"

sentences.zh: 延德曰：「禮亦不當拜。」

translations.literal: Yande said: "By ritual one should not bow there either."
translations.idiomatic: Yande answered: "Protocol does not require that either."

sentences.zh: 阿多於越復數日始相見，然其禮頗恭。

translations.literal: Aduoyuyue waited several more days before meeting them, yet his courtesy was quite respectful.
translations.idiomatic: Aduoyuyue delayed their meeting for several days, but when they met his courtesy was marked.

sentences.zh: 師子王邀延德至其北廷。

translations.literal: The Lion King invited Yande to his Beiting.
translations.idiomatic: The Lion King then invited Yande to join him at Beiting.

sentences.zh: 曆交河州，凡六日，至金嶺口，寶貨所出。

translations.literal: Passing through Jiaohe prefecture, in all six days they reached Jinding Pass, where precious goods were produced.
translations.idiomatic: They traveled through Jiaohe prefecture for six days until they reached Jinding Pass, a place where precious goods were sourced.

sentences.zh: 又兩日，至漢家砦。

translations.literal: Two more days, and they reached Hanjia Stockade.
translations.idiomatic: After two more days they arrived at Hanjia Stockade.

sentences.zh: 又五日，上金嶺。

translations.literal: Five more days, and they ascended Golden Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: Five days later they climbed Golden Ridge.

sentences.zh: 過嶺即多雨雪，嶺上有龍堂，刻石記雲，小雪山也。

translations.literal: Once past the ridge there was much rain and snow; on the ridge was a Dragon Hall with an inscription on stone saying it was the Little Snow Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the pass rain and snow were frequent. On the ridge stood a Dragon Hall; an inscription carved in stone declared the place the Little Snow Mountain.

sentences.zh: 嶺上有積雪，行人皆服毛罽。

translations.literal: On the ridge was accumulated snow; travelers all wore felt garments.
translations.idiomatic: Snow lay deep on the ridge, and every traveler wore felt clothing.

sentences.zh: 度嶺一日至北廷，憩高台寺。

translations.literal: Crossing the ridge in one day they reached Beiting and rested at Gaotai Temple.
translations.idiomatic: They crossed the pass in a day and reached Beiting, where they rested at Gaotai Temple.

sentences.zh: 其王烹羊馬以具膳，尤豐潔。

translations.literal: The king cooked sheep and horses to prepare the banquet, which was especially abundant and refined.
translations.idiomatic: The king had sheep and horses slaughtered for the feast, which was lavish and splendid.

sentences.zh: 地多馬，王及王後、太子各養馬，放牧平川中，彌亙百餘里，以毛色分別為群，莫知其數。

translations.literal: The land had many horses; the king, the queen, and the crown prince each kept horses, pasturing them on the flat plains for more than a hundred li, sorting them into herds by coat color — no one knew their number.
translations.idiomatic: Horses were abundant there. The king, queen, and crown prince each maintained herds pastured across the open plains for more than a hundred li, grouped by coat color in numbers beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 北廷川長廣數千里，鷹鷂雕鶻之所生，多美草，不生花，砂鼠大如<需免>，鷙禽捕食之。

translations.literal: The Beiting plain was several thousand li long and broad; hawks, kites, eagles, and falcons were born there. There was much fine grass but no flowers. Sand rats were as large as hares, which fierce birds seized and ate.
translations.idiomatic: The Beiting plain stretched thousands of li in every direction, a breeding ground for hawks, kites, eagles, and falcons. Fine grasses covered the land but no flowers grew. Sand rats as large as hares were hunted by raptors.

sentences.zh: 其王遣人來言，擇日以見使者，願無訝其淹久。

translations.literal: The king sent someone to say that he would choose a day to receive the envoy and hoped the envoy would not be surprised at the long delay.
translations.idiomatic: The king sent word that he would select a day to receive the envoy and asked that the delay not be taken amiss.

sentences.zh: 至七日，見其王及王子侍者，皆東向拜受賜。

translations.literal: On the seventh day they saw the king, princes, and attendants; all bowed facing east to receive gifts.
translations.idiomatic: On the seventh day the king, his princes, and their attendants appeared and all bowed facing east to receive the imperial gifts.

sentences.zh: 旁有持磬者擊以節拜，王聞磬聲乃拜，既而王之兒女親屬皆出，羅拜以受賜，遂張樂飲宴，為優戲，至暮。

translations.literal: Beside them were men holding chime-stones who struck them to mark the rhythm of the bows; the king bowed only upon hearing the chime. Then the king's sons, daughters, and kin all came out and bowed in rows to receive gifts; music was spread for a drinking feast and entertainers performed until evening.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants with chime-stones struck them to mark each bow; the king bowed only at the sound of the chime. Then his sons, daughters, and kinsmen came forth and bowed in rows to receive their gifts. A banquet followed with music and entertainers, and the revelry lasted until nightfall.

sentences.zh: 明日泛舟於池中，池四面作鼓樂。

translations.literal: The next day they boated on the pond, with drums and music on all four sides of the pond.
translations.idiomatic: The next day they took boats on the palace pond while drums and music sounded on every side.

sentences.zh: 又明日遊佛寺，曰應運太寧之寺，貞觀十四年造。

translations.literal: The day after that they visited a Buddhist temple called the Temple of Responding Fortune and Great Tranquility, built in the fourteenth year of Zhenguan.
translations.idiomatic: On the following day they visited a Buddhist temple called the Temple of Responding Fortune and Great Tranquility, built in the fourteenth year of the Zhenguan era.

sentences.zh: 北廷北山中出硇砂，山中嘗有煙氣湧起，無雲霧，至夕光焰若炬火，照見禽鼠皆赤。

translations.literal: Sal ammoniac came from the northern mountains of Beiting. Smoke often surged up in the mountains without cloud or mist; by evening the flames were like torches, and birds and rats seen in the light all appeared red.
translations.idiomatic: Sal ammoniac was mined in the mountains north of Beiting. Smoke often rose from the peaks without cloud or mist, and by evening the glow burned like torches, turning every bird and rat caught in its light blood-red.

sentences.zh: 采者著木底鞋取之，皮者即焦。

translations.literal: Gatherers wore wooden-soled shoes to take it; leather ones were scorched at once.
translations.idiomatic: Miners wore wooden-soled shoes to collect it; leather soles were scorched instantly.

sentences.zh: 下有穴生青泥，出穴外即變為砂石，土人取以治皮。

translations.literal: Below were caves producing blue mud; once outside the caves it turned into sand and stone. The local people took it to treat hides.
translations.idiomatic: Caves below yielded a blue mud that hardened into sand and gravel once exposed to air; locals used it to cure leather.

sentences.zh: 城中多樓台卉木。

translations.literal: In the city were many towers, terraces, flowers, and trees.
translations.idiomatic: The city abounded in towers, terraces, flowering plants, and trees.

sentences.zh: 人白皙端正，性工巧，善治金銀銅鐵為器及攻玉。

translations.literal: The people were fair-skinned and upright in bearing, skilled by nature, and good at working gold, silver, copper, and iron into vessels and at carving jade.
translations.idiomatic: The people were fair-complexioned and well favored, naturally dexterous and skilled at fashioning vessels from gold, silver, copper, and iron and at carving jade.

sentences.zh: 善馬直絹一匹，其駑馬充食，才直一丈。

translations.literal: A good horse was worth one bolt of silk; inferior horses used for food were worth only one zhang.
translations.idiomatic: A fine horse fetched one bolt of silk; a nag slaughtered for meat was worth only ten feet of cloth.

sentences.zh: 貧者皆食肉。

translations.literal: The poor all ate meat.
translations.idiomatic: Even the poor lived on meat.

sentences.zh: 西抵安西，即唐之西境。

translations.literal: To the west it reached Anxi — that is, Tang's western frontier.
translations.idiomatic: To the west it reached Anxi, the western border of Tang.

sentences.zh: 七月，令延德先還其國，其王九月始至。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Yande was ordered to return to his country first; the king did not arrive until the ninth month.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Yande was sent home ahead of the king, who did not arrive until the ninth month.

sentences.zh: 亦聞有契丹使來，謂其王云：「高敞本漢土，漢使來覘視封域，將有異圖，王當察之。」

translations.literal: It was also heard that a Khitan envoy had come and told the king: "Gaochang was originally Han territory. Han envoys have come to spy on the borders and will harbor other designs. The king should be on guard."
translations.idiomatic: Word also came that a Khitan envoy had told the king: "Gaochang was once Han soil. These Han envoys are here to reconnoiter your borders and surely mean you harm. Your Majesty should take heed."

sentences.zh: 延德偵知其語，因謂王曰：「契丹素不順中國，今乃反間，我欲殺之。」

translations.literal: Yande learned of these words by espionage and therefore said to the king: "The Khitan have never been loyal to the Middle Kingdom; now they sow discord. I wish to kill them."
translations.idiomatic: Yande learned of this through his own spies and told the king: "The Khitan have never been loyal to the Middle Kingdom. They are sowing discord, and I mean to kill them."

sentences.zh: 王固勸乃止。

translations.literal: The king firmly dissuaded him, and he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The king strongly dissuaded him, and Yande desisted.

sentences.zh: 自六年五月離京師，七年四月至高昌，所曆以詔賜諸國君長襲衣、金帶、繒帛。

translations.literal: From leaving the capital in the fifth month of the sixth year to reaching Gaochang in the fourth month of the seventh year, wherever they passed they bestowed by edict on the rulers of each state ceremonial robes, gold belts, and silks.
translations.idiomatic: From their departure from the capital in the fifth month of the sixth year until they reached Gaochang in the fourth month of the seventh year, they distributed imperial gifts of ceremonial robes, gold belts, and silks to every ruler they visited.

sentences.zh: 八年春，與其謝恩使凡百餘人復循舊路而還，雍熙元年四月至京師。

translations.literal: In the spring of the eighth year, together with their gratitude envoys, more than a hundred persons in all returned by the old route and reached the capital in the fourth month of the first year of Yongxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the eighth year more than a hundred men, including the gratitude envoys, retraced their route home and reached the capital in the fourth month of the first year of Yongxi.

sentences.zh: 景德元年，又遣使金延福來貢。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingde, they again sent the envoy Jin Yanfu with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jingde they again sent the envoy Jin Yanfu with tribute.

sentences.zh: 回鶻本匈奴之別裔，在天德西北娑陵水上。

translations.literal: The Uyghurs were originally a separate branch of the Xiongnu, on the Salian River northwest of Tiande.
