translations.idiomatic: The Uyghurs were originally a separate branch of the Xiongnu, living along the Salian River northwest of Tiande.

sentences.zh: 後魏號鐵勒，唐初號特勒，後稱回紇。

translations.literal: Under Later Wei they were called Tiele; in early Tang they were called Tele; later they were called Huihe.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Northern Wei they were known as the Tiele; in early Tang as the Tele; later they took the name Huihe.

sentences.zh: 其君長曰可汗，自貞觀以後朝貢不絕。

translations.literal: Their ruler was called khan; from the Zhenguan era onward court tribute never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Their ruler was styled khan, and from the Zhenguan era onward tribute missions to the court never ceased.

sentences.zh: 至德初，出兵助國討平安、史之亂，故累朝恩禮最重。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Zhide era they sent troops to help the state suppress the An and Shi rebellion, and for this successive dynasties showed them the greatest favor and ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Zhide era they sent troops to help suppress the An Lushan and Shi Siming rebellion, and for this successive dynasties treated them with the greatest favor.

sentences.zh: 然而恃功橫恣，朝廷雖患其邀求無厭，然頗姑息聽從之。

translations.literal: Yet relying on their merit they acted with arrogant license; although the court was troubled by their endless demands, it largely indulged and yielded to them.
translations.idiomatic: Yet emboldened by their service they grew arrogant and demanding; though the court resented their endless requests, it largely indulged them.

sentences.zh: 元和中，改為回鶻。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhe era the name was changed to Uyghur.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuanhe era their name was changed to Uyghur.

sentences.zh: 會昌中，其國衰亂，其相馺職者擁外甥將龐勒西奔安西。

translations.literal: In the Huichang era their state fell into decline and disorder; the chancellor Sa Zhizhe led the khan's nephew, the general Pang Le, west in flight to Anxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the Huichang era their state fell into turmoil; Chancellor Sa Zhizhe led the khan's nephew, General Pang Le, west in flight to Anxi.

sentences.zh: 既而回鶻為幽州張仲武所破，龐勒乃自稱可汗，居甘、沙、西州，無復昔時之盛矣。

translations.literal: Soon after the Uyghurs were broken by Zhang Zhongwu of Youzhou; Pang Le then styled himself khan and dwelt in Gan, Sha, and Xizhou, no longer possessing their former greatness.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after Zhang Zhongwu of Youzhou shattered the Uyghurs, Pang Le declared himself khan and settled in Ganzhou, Shazhou, and Xizhou, never again matching their former power.

sentences.zh: 歷梁、後唐、晉、漢、周，皆遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: Through Liang, Later Tang, Jin, Han, and Zhou they all sent envoys with court tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Through the Liang, Later Tang, Jin, Han, and Zhou dynasties they continued to send envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 後唐同光中，冊其國王仁美為英義可汗。

translations.literal: In the Tongguang era of Later Tang their king Renmei was enfeoffed as the Heroic and Righteous Khan.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tongguang era of Later Tang their king Renmei was invested as the Heroic and Righteous Khan.

sentences.zh: 仁美卒，其弟仁裕立，冊為順化可汗。

translations.literal: When Renmei died, his younger brother Renyu succeeded and was enfeoffed as the Compliant and Transforming Khan.
translations.idiomatic: When Renmei died his younger brother Renyu succeeded and was invested as the Compliant and Transforming Khan.

sentences.zh: 晉天福中，又改為奉化可汗。

translations.literal: In the Tianfu era of Jin he was again changed to the Obedient and Transforming Khan.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianfu era of Later Jin his title was changed to the Obedient and Transforming Khan.

sentences.zh: 仁裕卒，子景瓊立。

translations.literal: When Renyu died, his son Jingqiong succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Renyu died his son Jingqiong succeeded.

sentences.zh: 先是，唐朝繼以公主下嫁，故回鶻世稱中朝為舅，中朝每賜答詔亦曰外甥。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Tang dynasty had repeatedly sent princesses in marriage, so the Uyghurs always called the Middle Kingdom "uncle," and the Middle Kingdom in each responding edict also called them "nephew."
translations.idiomatic: Because the Tang had repeatedly sent princesses to marry Uyghur khans, the Uyghurs always addressed the Middle Kingdom as "uncle," and imperial edicts in reply addressed them as "nephew."

sentences.zh: 五代之後皆因之。

translations.literal: After the Five Dynasties this practice was followed in all cases.
translations.idiomatic: The Five Dynasties and their successors preserved the custom.

sentences.zh: 建隆二年，景瓊遣使朝獻。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianlong, Jingqiong sent envoys with court offerings.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianlong, Jingqiong sent envoys to court with tribute.

sentences.zh: 三年，阿都督等四十二人以方物來貢。

translations.literal: In the third year, Commander A and forty-two others came with local products as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Commander A and forty-two others arrived with local products as tribute.

sentences.zh: 乾德二年，遣使貢玉百團、琥珀四十斤，犛牛尾、貂鼠等。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qiande they sent envoys offering one hundred lumps of jade, forty jin of amber, yak tails, sable and rat-fur, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Qiande they sent envoys with one hundred lumps of jade, forty pounds of amber, yak tails, sable pelts, and the like.

sentences.zh: 三年，遣使趙黨誓等四十七人以團玉、琥珀、紅白犛牛尾為貢。

translations.literal: In the third year they sent envoys Zhao Dangshi and forty-seven others with lump jade, amber, and red and white yak tails as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year they sent Zhao Dangshi and forty-seven others with lump jade, amber, and red and white yak tails.

sentences.zh: 開寶中累遣使貢方物，其宰相鞠仙越亦貢馬。

translations.literal: In the Kaibao era they repeatedly sent envoys with local products as tribute; their chancellor Ju Xianyue also offered horses.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaibao era they sent tribute missions repeatedly, and their chancellor Ju Xianyue also presented horses.

sentences.zh: 太平興國二年冬，遣殿直張璨齎詔諭甘、沙州回鶻可汗外甥，賜以器幣，招致名馬美玉，以備車騎琮璜之用。

translations.literal: In the winter of the second year of Taiping Xingguo, Palace Attendant Zhang Can was dispatched bearing an edict to instruct the Uyghur khan, maternal nephew of Gan and Shazhou, granting vessels and gifts and seeking to obtain famous horses and fine jade for use in imperial carriages and ritual regalia.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the second year of Taiping Xingguo Palace Attendant Zhang Can was sent with an edict to the Uyghur khan of Ganzhou and Shazhou, styled the emperor's maternal nephew, granting gifts and seeking fine horses and jade for the imperial carriages and ritual regalia.

sentences.zh: 五年，甘、沙州回鶻可汗夜落紇密禮遏遣使裴溢的等四人，以橐駝、名馬、珊瑚、琥珀來獻。

translations.literal: In the fifth year the Uyghur khan of Gan and Shazhou, Yeluohe Milie, sent envoys Pei Yide and four others with camels, famous horses, coral, and amber as offerings.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year the Uyghur khan of Ganzhou and Shazhou, Yeluohe Milie, sent Pei Yide and three others with camels, fine horses, coral, and amber.

sentences.zh: 雍熙元年四月，西州回鶻與婆羅門僧永世、波斯外道阿里煙同入貢。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the first year of Yongxi, the Xizhou Uyghurs entered tribute together with the Brahman monk Yongshi and the Persian heterodox teacher Aliyan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the first year of Yongxi the Xizhou Uyghurs came to court together with the Brahman monk Yongshi and the Persian teacher Aliyan.

sentences.zh: 四年，合羅川回鶻第四族首領遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: In the fourth year the leader of the fourth tribe of the Heluo River Uyghurs sent envoys with court tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year the chief of the fourth tribe of the Heluo River Uyghurs sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 端拱二年九月，回鶻都督石仁政、麽囉王子、邈拿王子、越黜黃水州巡檢四族並居賀蘭山下，無所統屬，諸部入貢多由其地。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the second year of Duangong, the Uyghur commander Shi Renzheng, the Prince of Mola, the Prince of Yaona, and the four tribes of the Huangshui prefectural inspector Yuechu all dwelt beneath Helan Mountain without a common overlord; many tribes entering tribute passed through their lands.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the second year of Duangong the Uyghur commander Shi Renzheng, the Prince of Mola, the Prince of Yaona, and the four tribes under Huangshui inspector Yuechu all lived beneath Helan Mountain without a single overlord, and most tribute missions from the western tribes passed through their territory.

sentences.zh: 麽囉王子自雲，向為靈州馮暉阻絕，由是不通貢奉，今有內附意。

translations.literal: The Prince of Mola said himself that formerly Feng Hui of Lingzhou had blocked and cut him off, and for this reason tribute had not gotten through; now he wished to submit inwardly.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Mola declared that Feng Hui of Lingzhou had long blocked his routes, cutting off tribute missions, but that he now wished to submit to the court.

sentences.zh: 各以錦袍銀帶賜之。

translations.literal: Each was granted brocade robes and silver belts.
translations.idiomatic: Each was granted brocade robes and silver belts.

sentences.zh: 咸平四年，可汗王祿勝遣使曹萬通以玉勒名馬、獨峰無峰橐駝、賓鐵劍甲、琉璃器來貢。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xianping, Khan Wang Lusheng sent the envoy Cao Wantong with jade-bitted famous horses, single-humped and double-humped camels, guest-iron swords and armor, and glassware as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Xianping Khan Wang Lusheng sent Cao Wantong with jade-bitted horses, one-humped and two-humped camels, fine steel arms and armor, and glassware.

sentences.zh: 萬通自言任本國樞密使，本國東至黃河，西至雪山，有小郡數百，甲馬甚精習，願朝廷命使統領，使得縛繼遷以獻。

translations.literal: Wantong said himself that he held the post of privy commissioner in his state; his state extended east to the Yellow River and west to the Snow Mountains, with several hundred small districts, and its armored troops were very well trained. He wished the court to appoint an envoy to command them so that he might bind Li Jiqian and present him as a captive.
translations.idiomatic: Wantong declared that he served as privy commissioner of his state, which stretched from the Yellow River in the east to the Snow Mountains in the west and comprised several hundred districts with well-drilled cavalry. He asked the court to appoint an envoy to command his forces so that he might capture Li Jiqian and deliver him as a prisoner.

sentences.zh: 因降詔祿勝曰：「賊遷凶悖，人神所棄。

translations.literal: An edict was therefore issued to Lusheng saying: "The rebel Jiqian is vicious and defiant, abandoned by men and spirits alike.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was issued to Lusheng: "The rebel Jiqian is vicious and defiant, forsaken by men and gods alike.

sentences.zh: 卿世濟忠烈，義篤舅甥，繼上奏封，備陳方略，且欲大舉精甲，就覆殘妖，拓土西陲，獻俘北闕。

translations.literal: You for generations have continued loyalty and valor; the bond of uncle and nephew is deep. You repeatedly submitted memorials in sealed packets, fully setting forth strategy, and moreover wish to launch a great campaign with picked armor to overthrow the remnant demon, extend the western frontier, and present captives at the northern gate.
translations.idiomatic: Your house has served with loyalty across generations, and the bond of uncle and nephew runs deep. You have sent repeated sealed memorials setting forth your strategy, offering to march with picked troops against this remnant rebel, extend the western frontier, and present captives at the northern gate of the palace.

sentences.zh: 可汗功業，其可勝言！

translations.literal: The khan's achievements — how can they be fully told!
translations.idiomatic: Such service would be an achievement beyond words!

sentences.zh: 嘉歎所深，不忘朕意。

translations.literal: Our admiration is profound; do not forget Our intent.
translations.idiomatic: Our admiration runs deep; hold fast to Our intent.

sentences.zh: 今更不遣使臣，一切委卿統製。」

translations.literal: Now We shall send no further envoy; everything is entrusted to your command and control."
translations.idiomatic: We shall send no envoy; full command is entrusted to you."

sentences.zh: 特授萬通左神武軍大將軍，優賜祿勝器服。

translations.literal: Wantong was specially appointed Grand General of the Left Divine Martial Army, and Lusheng was generously granted vessels and robes.
translations.idiomatic: Wantong was specially appointed Grand General of the Left Divine Martial Army, and Lusheng received a generous grant of gifts and robes.

sentences.zh: 景德元年，夜落紇遣使來貢。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingde, Yeluohe sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jingde Yeluohe sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 四年，又遣尼法仙等來朝，獻馬。

translations.literal: In the fourth year they again sent the nun Faxiand and others to court, offering horses.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year they again sent the nun Faxiand and others to court with horses.

sentences.zh: 仍許法仙遊五臺山。

translations.literal: Faxian was also permitted to visit Mount Wutai.
translations.idiomatic: Faxian was also granted leave to visit Mount Wutai.

sentences.zh: 又遣僧翟入奏，來獻馬，欲於京城建佛寺祝聖壽，求賜名額，不許。

translations.literal: They also sent the monk Zhai to enter memorial, coming to offer horses and wishing to build a Buddhist temple in the capital to pray for the sage longevity; they requested a granted name plaque, but this was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: They also sent the monk Zhai to court with horses, asking permission to build a Buddhist temple in the capital to pray for the emperor's long life; the request for an imperial name plaque was denied.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符元年，夏州萬子等軍主領族兵趨回鶻，回鶻設伏要路，示弱不與闘，俟其過，奮起擊之，勦戮殆盡。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dazhong Xiangfu, Wanzi, army chief of Xiazhou, led tribal troops toward the Uyghurs; the Uyghurs set an ambush on a key road, feigned weakness and did not engage, waited until they had passed, then rose up and struck them, slaughtering nearly all.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Dazhong Xiangfu, Wanzi, army chief of Xiazhou, led tribal troops against the Uyghurs; the Uyghurs ambushed them on a key road, feigned weakness and held back, then attacked after they had passed and slaughtered nearly all.

sentences.zh: 其生擒者，回鶻驅坐於野，悉以所獲資粮示之，曰：「爾輩狐鼠，規求小利，我則不然。」

translations.literal: Those taken alive the Uyghurs drove to sit in the open field, showed them all the provisions they had captured, and said: "You are foxes and rats, scheming for petty gain — I am not like that."
translations.idiomatic: The captives were driven to sit in the open field while the Uyghurs displayed all the provisions they had seized and said: "You are foxes and rats scheming for petty gain — I am not like that."

sentences.zh: 遂盡焚而殺之，唯萬子軍主挺身走。

translations.literal: They then burned everything and killed them; only Army Chief Wanzi fled bodily.
translations.idiomatic: They then burned everything and killed them; only Army Chief Wanzi escaped.

sentences.zh: 鎮戎軍以聞，上曰：「回鶻嘗殺繼遷，世為讎敵。

translations.literal: Zhenrong Army reported it; the emperor said: "The Uyghurs once killed Jiqian and have been enemies for generations.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenrong Army reported the matter; the emperor said: "The Uyghurs once killed Jiqian and have been enemies for generations.

sentences.zh: 甘州使至，亦言德明侵軼之狀，意頗輕視之。

translations.literal: When the Ganzhou envoy arrived, he also spoke of Deming's raids and incursions, and the court was inclined to look down on them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ganzhou envoy arrived, he also described Deming's raids, and the court was inclined to underestimate them.

sentences.zh: 量其兵勢，德明未易敵也。」

translations.literal: Judging their military strength, Deming would not be easy to match."
translations.idiomatic: Judging their military strength, Deming would not be easy to match."

sentences.zh: 其年，夜落紇、寶物公主及沒孤公主、娑溫宰相各遣使來貢。

translations.literal: That year Yeluohe, Princess Baowu, Princess Moguo, and Chancellor Suowen each sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: That year Yeluohe, Princess Baowu, Princess Moguo, and Chancellor Suowen each sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 東封禮成，以可汗王進奉使姚進為寧遠將軍，寶物公主進奉曹進為安化郎將，賜以袍笏。

translations.literal: When the eastern feng rites were completed, tribute envoy Yao Jin of Khan Wang was made General of Pacifying the Distance, tribute envoy Cao Jin of Princess Baowu was made Gentleman of Tranquil Transformation, and robes and court tablets were granted.
translations.idiomatic: When the eastern feng rites were completed, Yao Jin, tribute envoy of Khan Wang, was made General of Pacifying the Distance, Cao Jin, tribute envoy of Princess Baowu, was made Gentleman of Tranquil Transformation, and robes and court tablets were granted.

sentences.zh: 又賜夜落紇介冑。

translations.literal: Yeluohe was also granted armor.
translations.idiomatic: Yeluohe was also granted armor.

sentences.zh: 三年，又遣左溫宰相、何居錄越樞密使、翟符守榮等來貢。

translations.literal: In the third year they again sent the left chancellor Zuowen, the privy commissioner He Jiluyue, Zhai Fushourong, and others with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year they again sent Left Chancellor Zuowen, Privy Commissioner He Jiluyue, Zhai Fushourong, and others with tribute.

sentences.zh: 是年，龜茲國王可汗遣使李延福、副使安福、監使翟進來進香藥、花蕊布、名馬、獨峰駝、大尾羊、玉鞍勒、琥珀、俞石等。

translations.literal: That year the king of Kucha, styled khan, sent the envoy Li Yanfu, vice-envoy An Fu, and supervising envoy Zhai Jin with fragrant medicines, flowered calico, famous horses, single-humped camels, long-tailed sheep, jade saddles and bits, amber, brass, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: That year the khan-king of Kucha sent Li Yanfu as envoy, An Fu as vice-envoy, and Zhai Jin as supervising envoy with fragrant medicines, flowered calico, fine horses, one-humped camels, long-tailed sheep, jade saddles and bits, amber, brass, and the like.

sentences.zh: 四年，翟符守榮等三十人請從祀汾陰。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Zhai Fushourong and thirty others requested to follow in the sacrifice at Fenyin.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Zhai Fushourong and thirty others asked to join the sacrifice at Fenyin.

sentences.zh: 其年，夜落紇遣使貢方物，秦州回鶻安密獻玉帶於道左。

translations.literal: That year Yeluohe sent envoys with local products as tribute; the Qinzhou Uyghur An Mi presented a jade belt by the roadside.
translations.idiomatic: That year Yeluohe sent envoys with tribute, and the Qinzhou Uyghur An Mi presented a jade belt along the route.

sentences.zh: 禮成，以翟符守榮為左神武軍大將軍，安殿民為保順郎將，餘皆賜冠帶器幣。

translations.literal: When the rites were completed, Zhai Fushourong was made Grand General of the Left Divine Martial Army, An Dianmin was made Langjiang of Baoshun, and the rest were all granted caps, belts, vessels, and gifts.
translations.idiomatic: When the rites were completed, Zhai Fushourong was appointed Grand General of the Left Divine Martial Army, An Dianmin was made Langjiang of Baoshun, and the rest received caps, belts, and gifts.

sentences.zh: 其年，夜落紇遣使言，敗趙德明立功首領請加恩賞。

translations.literal: That year Yeluohe sent envoys saying that the leaders who had achieved merit in defeating Zhao Deming requested increased favor and rewards.
translations.idiomatic: That year Yeluohe sent word that the leaders who had distinguished themselves in defeating Zhao Deming deserved additional honors.

sentences.zh: 詔給司戈、司階、郎將告敕十道，使得承製補署。

translations.literal: An edict granted ten commissions as Sigge, Sijie, and Langjiang so that they might receive imperial appointment and be assigned to posts.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted ten commissions as Sigge, Sijie, and Langjiang, authorizing the khan to appoint men to those ranks.

sentences.zh: 六年，龜茲進奉使李延慶等三十六人對於長春殿，獻名馬、弓箭、鞍勒、團玉、香藥等，優詔答之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year the Kucha tribute envoys Li Yanqing and thirty-six others were received in audience at the Changchun Hall, presenting famous horses, bows and arrows, saddles and bits, lump jade, fragrant medicines, and the like; a gracious edict replied to them.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year the Kucha tribute envoys Li Yanqing and thirty-six others were received at the Changchun Hall with fine horses, bows and arrows, saddles and bits, lump jade, and fragrant medicines; the emperor replied with a gracious edict.

sentences.zh: 先是，甘州數與夏州接戰，夜落紇貢奉多為夏州鈔奪。

translations.literal: Earlier, Ganzhou had repeatedly fought border battles with Xiazhou, and much of Yeluohe's tribute was plundered by Xiazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Previously Ganzhou had fought repeatedly with Xiazhou, and many of Yeluohe's tribute missions were raided by Xiazhou forces.

sentences.zh: 及宗哥族感悅朝廷恩化，乃遣人援送其使，故頻年得至京師。

translations.literal: When the Zongge tribe came to appreciate the court's gracious transforming influence, they sent men to escort and convey the envoys, and for this reason in successive years they were able to reach the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zongge tribe came to appreciate the court's benevolence, they sent escorts to convey the envoys safely, and for several years the missions reached the capital.

sentences.zh: 既而唃廝羅欲娶可汗女而無聘財，可汗不許，因為仇敵。

translations.literal: Soon after, Gusiluo wished to marry the khan's daughter but had no betrothal gifts; the khan would not agree, and for this reason they became enemies.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, Gusiluo sought to marry the khan's daughter but could offer no bride-price; the khan refused, and the two became enemies.

sentences.zh: 五年，秦州遣指揮使楊知進、譯者郭敏送進奉使至甘州，會宗哥怨隙阻歸路，遂留知進等不敢遣。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Qinzhou dispatched Commandant Yang Zhijin and interpreter Guo Min to escort the tribute envoys to Ganzhou; encountering the Zongge tribe's grievance and enmity blocking the return route, they detained Zhijin and the others and did not dare send them back.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Qinzhou dispatched Commandant Yang Zhijin and interpreter Guo Min to escort the tribute envoys to Ganzhou. The Zongge tribe's enmity blocked the return route, and the khan detained Zhijin and his party, not daring to send them home.

sentences.zh: 八年，敏方得還。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Min was finally able to return.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year Guo Min was at last able to return.

sentences.zh: 可汗王夜落隔上表言寶物公主疾死，以西涼人蘇守信劫亂，不時奏聞；

translations.literal: Khan Wang Yeluohe submitted a memorial saying that Princess Baowu had died of illness, and because the Xiliang man Su Shouxin had seized and plundered in disorder, he had not reported it in timely fashion;
translations.idiomatic: Khan Wang Yeluohe submitted a memorial reporting that Princess Baowu had died of illness and explaining that turmoil raised by Su Shouxin of Xiliang had prevented timely notice;

sentences.zh: 又謝恩賜寶鈿、銀匣、曆日及安撫詔書，仍乞慰諭宗哥，使開朝貢之路。

translations.literal: he also thanked them for the grant of jeweled hairpins, silver caskets, calendars, and reassuring edicts, and still begged that the Zongge be comforted and instructed so as to open the route of court tribute.
translations.idiomatic: he thanked the court for jeweled hairpins, silver caskets, calendars, and reassuring edicts, and begged that the Zongge be mollified so that the tribute route might be reopened.

sentences.zh: 九年，楊知進亦至，遂遣郭敏賜宗哥詔書並甘州可汗器幣。

translations.literal: In the ninth year Yang Zhijin also arrived; Guo Min was then dispatched to grant the Zongge an edict together with vessels and gifts for the Ganzhou khan.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year Yang Zhijin also returned, and Guo Min was sent with an edict for the Zongge and gifts for the Ganzhou khan.

sentences.zh: 其年，使來朝貢，言夜落隔卒，九宰相諸部落奉夜落隔歸化為可汗王領國事。

translations.literal: That year envoys came to court with tribute, saying that Yeluohe had died and that the nine chancellors and various tribes had installed Yeluohe Guihua as khan-king to administer state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: That year tribute envoys reported that Yeluohe had died and that the nine chancellors and allied tribes had raised Yeluohe Guihua to khan-king to govern the realm.

sentences.zh: 天禧二年，夜落隔歸化遣都督安信等來朝。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianxi, Yeluohe Guihua sent Commander An Xin and others to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianxi Yeluohe Guihua sent Commander An Xin and others to court.

sentences.zh: 四年，又遣使同龜茲國可汗王智海使來獻大尾羊。

translations.literal: In the fourth year they again sent envoys together with the Kucha khan-king Wang Zhihai's envoys to present long-tailed sheep.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year they again sent envoys jointly with the mission of Kucha's khan-king Wang Zhihai, presenting long-tailed sheep.

sentences.zh: 初，回鶻西奔，族種散處。

translations.literal: At first, when the Uyghurs fled westward, the clans and peoples scattered and settled in separate places.
translations.idiomatic: When the Uyghurs fled westward their clans scattered across the frontier.

sentences.zh: 故甘州有可汗王，西州有克韓王，新復州有黑韓王，皆其後焉。

translations.literal: Therefore in Ganzhou there was a khan-king, in Xizhou a Kehan-king, and in Xinfu prefecture a Heihan-king — all were their descendants.
translations.idiomatic: Hence Ganzhou had its khan-king, Xizhou its Kehan-king, and Xinfu prefecture its Heihan-king — all descendants of the old Uyghur line.

sentences.zh: 天聖元年五月，甘州夜落隔通順遣使阿葛之、王文貴來貢方物。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the first year of Tiansheng, the Ganzhou Yeluohe Tongshun sent envoys A Gezhi and Wang Wengui with local products as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the first year of Tiansheng the Ganzhou ruler Yeluohe Tongshun sent A Gezhi and Wang Wengui with tribute.

sentences.zh: 六月，詔甘州回紇外甥可汗王夜落隔通順特封歸忠保順可汗王。

translations.literal: In the sixth month an edict specially enfeoffed the Ganzhou Huihe khan-king, maternal nephew Yeluohe Tongshun, as the Loyal and Obedient Khan-King.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month an edict specially invested the Ganzhou Uyghur khan-king, styled the emperor's maternal nephew, Yeluohe Tongshun, as the Loyal and Obedient Khan-King.

sentences.zh: 二年五月，遣使都督習信等十四人來貢馬及黃湖綿、細白氎。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the second year they sent envoys Commander Xixin and fourteen others with horses, yellow lake cotton, and fine white felt as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the second year they sent Commander Xixin and fourteen others with horses, yellow lake cotton, and fine white felt.

sentences.zh: 三年四月，可汗王、公主及宰相撒溫訛進馬、乳香。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the third year the khan-king, the princess, and Chancellor Sawen'e presented horses and frankincense.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the third year the khan-king, the princess, and Chancellor Sawen'e sent horses and frankincense.

sentences.zh: 賜銀器、金帶、衣著、暈錦旋襴有差。

translations.literal: Silver vessels, gold belts, garments, and halo-brocade spiral robes were granted in varying measure.
translations.idiomatic: They received graded gifts of silver vessels, gold belts, robes, and halo-brocade spiral gowns.

sentences.zh: 五年八月，遣使安萬東等一十四人來貢方物。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the fifth year they sent envoys An Wandong and fourteen others with local products as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the fifth year they sent An Wandong and fourteen others with tribute.

sentences.zh: 六年二月，遣人貢方物。

translations.literal: In the second month of the sixth year they sent men with local products as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the sixth year they sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 熙寧元年入貢，求買金字《大般若經》，以墨本賜之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xining they entered tribute, requesting to purchase the gold-letter Great Prajna Sutra; an ink copy was granted to them.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xining they came with tribute, asking to purchase a gold-letter edition of the Great Prajna Sutra; the court granted them an ink copy instead.

sentences.zh: 六年復來，補其首領五人為軍主，歲給彩二十匹。

translations.literal: In the sixth year they came again; five of their leaders were appointed army chiefs and granted twenty bolts of colored silk annually.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year they returned; five of their leaders were appointed army chiefs and granted twenty bolts of colored silk each year.

sentences.zh: 神宗問其國種落生齒幾何，曰三十餘萬；

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong asked how many clans and persons by birth were in their state; they said more than three hundred thousand;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenzong asked how many people their state numbered; they answered more than three hundred thousand;

sentences.zh: 壯可用者幾何，曰二十萬。

translations.literal: how many able-bodied men could be used; they said two hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: and how many were able-bodied men fit for service; they said two hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 明年，敕李憲擇使聘阿裏骨，使諭回鶻令發兵深入夏境。

translations.literal: The next year, an edict ordered Li Xian to choose an envoy to mission to Aligu and instruct the Uyghurs to send troops deep into Xia territory.
translations.idiomatic: The next year an edict ordered Li Xian to select an envoy to treat with Aligu and instruct the Uyghurs to dispatch troops deep into Western Xia territory.

sentences.zh: 憲以命殿直皇甫旦。

translations.literal: Xian assigned the mission to Director Palace Aide Huangfu Dan.
translations.idiomatic: Xian assigned the mission to the palace aide Huangfu Dan.

sentences.zh: 旦往，不得前而妄奏功狀，詔逮旦赴御史獄抵罪。

translations.literal: Dan went but could not advance yet falsely submitted a report of achievements; an edict ordered Dan arrested and sent to the censorate prison to answer for his crime.
translations.idiomatic: Dan set out but was unable to proceed yet falsely reported success; an edict ordered him arrested and sent to the censorate prison to answer for the offense.

sentences.zh: 然回鶻使不常來，宣和中，間因入貢散而之陝西諸州，公為貿易，至留久不歸。

translations.literal: Yet Uyghur envoys did not come regularly; in the Xuanhe era, occasionally when entering tribute they dispersed to various Shaanxi prefectures and openly traded, until they stayed long and did not return.
translations.idiomatic: Uyghur envoys nonetheless did not come regularly; during the Xuanhe period they sometimes scattered to various Shaanxi prefectures after entering tribute to trade openly, and stayed so long they failed to return.

sentences.zh: 朝廷慮其習知邊事，且往來皆經夏國，於播傳非便，乃立法禁之。

translations.literal: The court feared they had learned border affairs, and moreover their comings and goings all passed through the Xia state, inconvenient for intelligence transmission; thus a law was enacted to forbid it.
translations.idiomatic: The court feared they were learning border secrets, and since their routes all passed through Western Xia, which was inconvenient for communications, it enacted a prohibition.

sentences.zh: 大食國本波斯之別種。

translations.literal: The Dashi state was originally a separate branch of Persia.
translations.idiomatic: The state of Dashi was originally an offshoot of Persia.

sentences.zh: 隋大業中，波斯有桀黠者探穴得文石，以為瑞，乃糾合其眾，剽略資貨，聚徒浸盛，遂自立為王，據有波斯國之西境。

translations.literal: In the Daye era of Sui, in Persia a fierce and cunning man explored a cave and obtained patterned stone, taking it as an auspicious sign; he then gathered his followers, plundered goods, assembled followers gradually growing stronger, and thus set himself up as king, seizing the western lands of Persia.
translations.idiomatic: During the Sui dynasty's Daye era, a fierce and cunning man in Persia dug into a cave and found patterned stone, which he took as a portent; rallying followers he began raiding goods, his band growing ever stronger until he proclaimed himself king and seized the western regions of Persia.

sentences.zh: 唐永徽以後，屢來朝貢。

translations.literal: After the Yonghui era of Tang, they repeatedly came to court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: After Tang's Yonghui era they repeatedly sent tribute missions to court.

sentences.zh: 其王盆泥未換之前謂之白衣大食，阿蒲羅拔之後謂之黑衣大食。

translations.literal: Before their king Pannimiwan it was called the White-Robed Dashi; after Abu al-Abbas it was called the Black-Robed Dashi.
translations.idiomatic: Before the reign of King Pannimiwan it was known as the White-Robed Dashi; after Abu al-Abbas it was known as the Black-Robed Dashi.

sentences.zh: 乾德四年，僧行勤遊西域，因賜其王書以招懷之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Qiande, the monk Xingqin traveled the Western Regions, and on that account an imperial letter was granted to their king to win him over.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Qiande the monk Xingqin traveled the Western Regions, and the court granted their king an imperial letter to win his allegiance.

sentences.zh: 開寶元年，遣使來朝貢。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaibao, they sent envoys to court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Kaibao they sent envoys to court with tribute.

sentences.zh: 四年，又貢方物，以其使李訶末為懷化將軍，特以金花五色綾紙寫官告以賜。

translations.literal: In the fourth year they again presented local products as tribute; their envoy Li Hemo was appointed General Who Cherishes Transformation, and an appointment patent was specially written on five-colored brocade paper with gold floral patterns and granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year they again sent tribute; their envoy Li Hemo was appointed General Who Cherishes Transformation, and an appointment patent was specially written on gold-flowered five-colored brocade paper and granted to him.

sentences.zh: 是年，本國及占城、闍婆又致禮物於李煜。

translations.literal: That year their state, together with Champa and Java, also sent gifts to Li Yu.
translations.idiomatic: That year Dashi, Champa, and Java also sent gifts to Li Yu.

sentences.zh: 煜不敢受，遣使來上，因詔自今勿以為獻。

translations.literal: Yu dared not accept and sent envoys to present them to the throne; an edict was therefore issued that from now on such gifts should not be offered.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yu dared not accept them and sent envoys to offer them to the throne; an edict was therefore issued that such gifts should no longer be presented.

sentences.zh: 六年，遣使來貢方物。

translations.literal: In the sixth year they sent envoys with local products as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year they sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 七年，國王訶黎佛又遣使不囉海，九年又遣使蒲希密，皆以方物來貢。

translations.literal: In the seventh year King Helifo again sent the envoy Buluohai; in the ninth year they again sent the envoy Puximi — all with local products as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year King Helifo again sent the envoy Buluohai; in the ninth year they again sent the envoy Puximi — each bearing tribute.

sentences.zh: 太平興國二年，遣使蒲思那、副使摩訶末、判官蒲囉等貢方物。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiping Xingguo, they sent the envoy Pusina, Vice-Envoy Mohemo, and Administrator Pula and others with local products as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taiping Xingguo they sent the envoy Pusina, Vice-Envoy Mohemo, Administrator Pula, and others with tribute.

sentences.zh: 其從者目深體黑，謂之昆侖奴。

translations.literal: Their attendants had deep-set eyes and dark bodies and were called Kunlun slaves.
translations.idiomatic: Their attendants, with deep-set eyes and dark skin, were called Kunlun slaves.

sentences.zh: 詔賜其使襲衣、器幣，從者縑帛有差。

translations.literal: An edict granted the envoys ceremonial robes and ritual vessels; attendants received silk in varying amounts.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted the envoys ceremonial robes and ritual gifts; their attendants received graded allotments of silk.

sentences.zh: 四年，復有朝貢使至。

translations.literal: In the fourth year tribute envoys again arrived.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year another tribute mission arrived.

sentences.zh: 雍熙元年，國人花茶來獻花錦、越諾、揀香、白龍腦、白沙糖、薔薇水、琉璃器。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongxi, a countryman named Huacha came and presented flowered brocade, yuenuo, selected incense, white dragon's-brain camphor, white sugar, rose water, and glassware.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongxi a countryman named Huacha came and presented flowered brocade, yuenuo cloth, selected incense, white dragon's-brain camphor, white sugar, rose water, and glassware.

sentences.zh: 淳化四年，又遣其副酋長李亞勿來貢。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chunhua, they again sent their vice-chieftain Li Yawu with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Chunhua they again sent their vice-chieftain Li Yawu with tribute.

sentences.zh: 其國舶主蒲希密至南海，以老病不能詣闕，乃以方物附亞勿來獻。

translations.literal: Their country's shipmaster Puximi reached the Southern Sea; because of old age and illness he could not go to court, and so sent local products with Yawu to present as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Their shipmaster Puximi reached the Southern Sea; too old and ill to go to court himself, he sent his goods with Yawu to present as tribute.

sentences.zh: 其表曰：

translations.literal: His memorial read:
translations.idiomatic: His memorial read:

sentences.zh: 大食舶主臣蒲希密上言，眾星垂象，回拱於北辰；

translations.literal: The Dashi shipmaster, your subject Puximi, respectfully states: the myriad stars hang their signs, circling back to the North Star;
translations.idiomatic: The Dashi shipmaster, your subject Puximi, respectfully states: the myriad stars hang their signs, wheeling about the North Star;

sentences.zh: 百穀疏源，委輸於東海。

translations.literal: the hundred grains spread their sources, flowing into the Eastern Sea.
translations.idiomatic: the hundred grains spread their sources, flowing toward the Eastern Sea.

sentences.zh: 屬有道之柔遠，罄無外以宅心。

translations.literal: At a time when the Way holds sway and distant lands are embraced, all beyond is gathered into the heart.
translations.idiomatic: In an age when the Way holds sway and distant lands are embraced, all beyond the realm is gathered into your heart.

sentences.zh: 伏惟皇帝陛下德合二儀，明齊七政，仁宥萬國，光被四夷。

translations.literal: I humbly consider that Your Majesty's virtue joins the two principles, your brilliance matches the seven regulators, your benevolence shelters the myriad states, and your radiance covers the four barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly consider that Your Majesty's virtue joins heaven and earth, your brilliance matches the seven luminaries, your benevolence shelters the myriad states, and your radiance covers the four quarters.

sentences.zh: 賡歌洽《擊壤》之民，重譯走奉珍之貢。

translations.literal: Songs of praise harmonize with the people of "Striking the Earth"; repeated translation brings envoys rushing to offer precious tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Songs of praise harmonize with the people of "Striking the Earth"; through repeated translation envoys rush to offer precious tribute.

sentences.zh: 臣顧惟殊俗，景慕中區，早傾向日之心，頗鬱朝天之願。

translations.literal: Your subject, considering my alien customs, admires the Central Region; long have I inclined a heart toward the sun, yet greatly have I been troubled in my wish to behold the court.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject, though of alien customs, admires the Central Region; long have I inclined my heart toward the sun, yet greatly have I been troubled in my wish to behold the court.

sentences.zh: 昨在本國，曾得廣州蕃長寄書招諭，令入京貢奉，盛稱皇帝聖德，布寬大之澤，詔下廣南，寵綏蕃商，阜通遠物。

translations.literal: Previously in my own country I received a letter from the Guangzhou foreign chief inviting and instructing me to enter the capital with tribute, greatly praising the emperor's sagely virtue, spreading a broad and generous grace; an edict was issued to Guangnan, favoring and soothing foreign merchants, enriching and opening distant goods.
translations.idiomatic: Previously in my own country I received a letter from the Guangzhou foreign chief inviting me to enter the capital with tribute, greatly praising the emperor's sagely virtue and spreading a broad and generous grace; an edict was issued to Guangnan favoring and soothing foreign merchants and enriching trade in distant goods.

sentences.zh: 臣遂乘海舶，爰率土毛，涉曆龍王之宮，瞻望天帝之境，庶遵玄化，以慰宿心。

translations.literal: Your subject then took a seagoing vessel, leading local products, passing through the palace of the Dragon King, gazing toward the domain of the Heavenly Emperor, hoping to follow the profound transformation and soothe my long-held heart.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject then took a seagoing vessel, bearing local products, passing through the palace of the Dragon King and gazing toward the domain of the Heavenly Emperor, hoping to follow the profound transformation and soothe my long-held heart.

sentences.zh: 今則雖屆五羊之城，猶賒雙鳳之闕。

translations.literal: Now though I have reached the city of Five Rams, I am still short of the Double-Phoenix Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Now though I have reached the city of Five Rams, I am still short of the Double-Phoenix Gate.

sentences.zh: 自念衰老，病不能興，遐想金門，心目俱斷。

translations.literal: Reflecting that I am aged and ill and cannot rise, gazing longingly toward the Golden Gate, my eyes and heart are both cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Reflecting that I am aged and ill and cannot rise, gazing longingly toward the Golden Gate, my eyes and heart are both cut off.

sentences.zh: 今遇李亞勿來貢，謹備蕃錦藥物附以上獻。

translations.literal: Now encountering Li Yawu coming with tribute, I respectfully prepare foreign brocades and medicines to attach and present above.
translations.idiomatic: Now that Li Yawu has come with tribute, I respectfully attach foreign brocades and medicines for presentation.

sentences.zh: 臣希密凡進象牙五十株，乳香千八百斤，賓鐵七百斤，紅絲吉貝一段，五色雜花蕃錦四段，白越諾二段，都爹一琉璃瓶，無名異一塊，薔薇水百瓶。

translations.literal: Your subject Puximi in all presented fifty tusks of ivory, one thousand eight hundred jin of frankincense, seven hundred jin of precious iron, one length of red silk and cotton cloth, four lengths of five-colored mixed-flower foreign brocade, two lengths of white yuenuo, one glass bottle of dudie, one piece of wumingyi, and one hundred bottles of rose water.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject Puximi in all presented fifty tusks of ivory, one thousand eight hundred jin of frankincense, seven hundred jin of precious iron, one length of red silk and cotton cloth, four lengths of five-colored mixed-flower foreign brocade, two lengths of white yuenuo, one glass bottle of dudie, one piece of wumingyi, and one hundred bottles of rose water.

sentences.zh: 詔賜希密敕書、錦袍、銀器、束帛等以答之。

translations.literal: An edict granted Puximi an imperial letter, brocade robe, silver vessels, bundles of silk, and the like in reply.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted Puximi an imperial letter, a brocade robe, silver vessels, bundles of silk, and the like in reply.

sentences.zh: 至道元年，其國舶主蒲押陀黎齎蒲希密表來獻白龍腦一百兩，膃肭臍五十對，龍鹽一銀合，眼藥二十小琉璃瓶，白沙糖三琉璃甕，千年棗、舶上五味子各六琉璃瓶，舶上褊桃一琉璃瓶，薔薇水二十琉璃瓶，乳香山子一坐，蕃錦二段，駝毛褥麵三段，白越諾三段。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhidao, their country's shipmaster Pu Yatuali brought Puximi's memorial and presented one hundred liang of white dragon's-brain camphor, fifty pairs of musk pods, one silver casket of dragon salt, twenty small glass bottles of eye medicine, three glass jars of white sugar, six glass bottles each of thousand-year jujubes and shipboard schisandra, one glass bottle of shipboard flat peaches, twenty glass bottles of rose water, one frankincense mountain seat, two lengths of foreign brocade, three camel-hair quilt covers, and three lengths of white yuenuo.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhidao their shipmaster Pu Yatuali brought Puximi's memorial and presented one hundred liang of white dragon's-brain camphor, fifty pairs of musk pods, one silver casket of dragon salt, twenty small glass bottles of eye medicine, three glass jars of white sugar, six glass bottles each of thousand-year jujubes and shipboard schisandra, one glass bottle of shipboard flat peaches, twenty glass bottles of rose water, one frankincense mountain seat, two lengths of foreign brocade, three camel-hair quilt covers, and three lengths of white yuenuo.

sentences.zh: 引對於崇政殿，譯者代奏云：「父蒲希密因緣射利，泛舶至廣州，迨今五稔未歸。

translations.literal: He was led in audience at the Chongzheng Hall; the interpreter submitted on his behalf, saying: "My father Puximi, seeking profit by chance, sailed to Guangzhou and for five years now has not returned.
translations.idiomatic: He was led in audience at the Chongzheng Hall; the interpreter submitted on his behalf, saying: "My father Puximi, seeking profit by chance, sailed to Guangzhou and for five years now has not returned.

sentences.zh: 母令臣遠來尋訪、昉至廣州見之。

translations.literal: My mother ordered your subject to come from afar to seek him; upon reaching Guangzhou I saw him.
translations.idiomatic: My mother ordered me to come from afar to seek him; upon reaching Guangzhou I saw him.

sentences.zh: 具言前歲蒙皇帝聖恩降敕書，賜以法錦袍、紫綾纏頭、間塗金銀鳳瓶一對、綾絹二十匹。

translations.literal: He fully stated that in the previous year he received the emperor's sagely grace in the form of a lowered imperial letter, granted a patterned brocade robe, purple silk headwrap, one pair of gold-inlaid silver phoenix bottles, and twenty bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: He fully stated that in the previous year he received the emperor's sagely grace in the form of an imperial letter, along with a patterned brocade robe, a purple silk headwrap, one pair of gold-inlaid silver phoenix bottles, and twenty bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 今令臣奉章來謝，以方物致貢。」

translations.literal: Now he has ordered your subject to bring a memorial to give thanks and to present local products as tribute."
translations.idiomatic: Now he has ordered me to bring a memorial to give thanks and to present local products as tribute."

sentences.zh: 太宗因問其國，對云：「與大秦國相鄰，為其統屬。

translations.literal: Taizong then asked about their country; they replied, saying: "It borders the Great Qin state and is subject to it.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong then asked about their country; they replied: "It borders the Great Qin state and is subject to it.

sentences.zh: 今本國所管之民才及數千，有都城介山海間。」

translations.literal: Now the people under this state's jurisdiction number only a few thousand; it has a capital city between mountains and sea."
translations.idiomatic: The people under our jurisdiction number only a few thousand; we have a capital city between mountains and sea."

sentences.zh: 又問其山澤所出，對云：「惟犀象香藥。」

translations.literal: He again asked what its mountains and marshes produced; they replied, saying: "Only rhinoceros, elephants, incense, and medicines."
translations.idiomatic: He again asked what its mountains and marshes produced; they replied: "Only rhinoceros, elephants, incense, and medicines."

sentences.zh: 問犀象以何法可取，對云：「象用象媒誘至，漸以大繩羈縻之耳；

translations.literal: Asked by what method rhinoceros and elephants could be taken, they replied, saying: "For elephants, an elephant decoy is used to lure them near, then gradually they are bound with large ropes;
translations.idiomatic: Asked by what method rhinoceros and elephants could be taken, they replied: "For elephants, an elephant decoy is used to lure them near, then they are gradually bound with large ropes;

sentences.zh: 犀則使人升大樹操弓矢，伺其至射而殺之，其小者不用弓矢可以捕獲。」

translations.literal: for rhinoceros, men climb tall trees with bows and arrows, wait for them to arrive, shoot and kill them — the small ones can be captured without bow and arrow."
translations.idiomatic: for rhinoceros, men climb tall trees with bows and arrows, wait for them to arrive, and shoot them — the small ones can be captured without bow and arrow."

sentences.zh: 上賜以襲衣、冠帶、被褥等物，令閣門宴犒訖，就館，延留數月遣回；

translations.literal: The emperor granted ceremonial robes, caps and belts, bedding, and the like, ordered the Gate Office to feast and reward them, then lodged them; after several months of extended stay they were sent back;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor granted ceremonial robes, caps and belts, bedding, and the like, ordered the Gate Office to feast and reward them, then lodged them; after several months of extended stay they were sent back;

sentences.zh: 降詔答賜蒲希密黃金，準其所貢之直。

translations.literal: an edict was issued in reply granting Puximi gold equal to the value of what he had presented as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: an edict was issued in reply granting Puximi gold equal to the value of his tribute.

sentences.zh: 三年二月，又與賓同隴國使來朝。

translations.literal: In the second month of the third year, they again came to court together with envoys from the Bin Tonglong state.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the third year they again came to court together with envoys from the Bin Tonglong state.

sentences.zh: 咸平二年，又遣判官文戊至。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianping, they again sent Administrator Wen Wu.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xianping they again sent Administrator Wen Wu.

sentences.zh: 三年，舶主陀婆離遣使穆吉鼻來貢。

translations.literal: In the third year, shipmaster Tuopoli sent the envoy Mujibi with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year shipmaster Tuopoli sent the envoy Mujibi with tribute.

sentences.zh: 吉鼻還，賜陀婆離詔書並器服鞍馬。

translations.literal: When Mujibi returned, Tuopoli was granted an imperial letter together with vessels, robes, saddle, and horse.
translations.idiomatic: When Mujibi returned, Tuopoli was granted an imperial letter together with vessels, robes, a saddle, and a horse.

sentences.zh: 六年，又遣使婆羅欽三摩尼等來貢方物。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, they again sent envoys Boluoqin Sanmoni and others with local products as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year they again sent Boluoqin Sanmoni and others with tribute.

sentences.zh: 摩尼等對於崇政殿，持真珠以進，自雲離國日誠願得瞻威顏即獻此，乞不給回賜。

translations.literal: Moni and the others were received at the Chongzheng Hall; holding pearls they presented them, stating of themselves that from the day they left their country they had wished to behold the august countenance and would present these; they begged not to be given return gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Sanmoni and the others were received at the Chongzheng Hall; holding pearls they presented them, stating that from the day they left their country they had wished to behold the august countenance and would present these; they begged not to be given return gifts.

sentences.zh: 真宗不欲違其意，俟其還，優加恩齎。

translations.literal: Zhenzong did not wish to go against their wish; when they returned he would generously add further favors.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzong did not wish to go against their wish; when they returned he would generously add further favors.

sentences.zh: 景德元年，又遣使來。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingde, they again sent envoys.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jingde they again sent envoys.

sentences.zh: 時與三佛齊、蒲端國使並在京師，會上元觀燈，皆賜錢縱其宴飲。

translations.literal: At that time their envoys were in the capital together with envoys from Srivijaya and Butuan; on the Lantern Festival they were all granted money and allowed to feast and drink freely.
translations.idiomatic: At that time their envoys were in the capital together with envoys from Srivijaya and Butuan; on the Lantern Festival the court granted them money and allowed them to feast freely.

sentences.zh: 其秋，蕃客蒲加心至。

translations.literal: That autumn the foreign guest Pu Jiaxin arrived.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn the foreign guest Pu Jiaxin arrived.

sentences.zh: 四年，又遣使同占城使來，優加館餼之禮，許徧至苑囿寺觀遊覽。

translations.literal: In the fourth year they again sent envoys together with Champa envoys; they were generously granted lodging and provisions, and were permitted to visit gardens, parks, temples, and monasteries throughout the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year they again sent envoys together with Champa envoys; they received generous lodging and provisions and were permitted to visit gardens, parks, temples, and monasteries throughout the capital.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符元年十月，車駕東封，舶主陀婆離上言願執方物赴泰山，從之。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the first year of Dazhong Xiangfu, when the imperial carriage went east to perform the feng sacrifice, shipmaster Tuopoli submitted a statement wishing to carry local products to Mount Tai; the request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the first year of Dazhong Xiangfu, when the imperial carriage went east to perform the feng sacrifice, shipmaster Tuopoli submitted a statement wishing to carry local products to Mount Tai; the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 又舶主李亞勿遣使麻勿來獻玉圭。

translations.literal: Also shipmaster Li Yawu sent the envoy Mawu to present a jade scepter.
translations.idiomatic: Shipmaster Li Yawu also sent the envoy Mawu to present a jade scepter.

sentences.zh: 並優賜器幣、袍帶，並賜國主銀飾繩床、水罐、器械、旗幟、鞍勒馬等。

translations.literal: All were generously granted vessels and ritual gifts, robes and belts; the ruler of their state was also granted a silver-decorated rope bed, water jar, weapons, banners and flags, saddle and bridle, and horse.
translations.idiomatic: All were generously granted vessels and ritual gifts, robes and belts; their ruler was also granted a silver-decorated rope bed, water jar, weapons, banners and flags, a saddle and bridle, and a horse.

sentences.zh: 四年祀汾陰，又遣歸德將軍陀羅離進瓶香、象牙、琥珀、無名異、繡絲、紅絲、碧黃綿、細越諾、紅駝毛、間金線璧衣、碧白琉璃酒器、薔薇水、千年棗等。

translations.literal: In the fourth year when sacrifices were performed at Fenyin, they again sent General Who Cherishes Virtue Tuoluoli with bottle incense, ivory, amber, wumingyi, embroidered silk, red silk, green and yellow cotton, fine yuenuo, red camel hair, gold-threaded jade garments, green and white glass wine vessels, rose water, thousand-year jujubes, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year when sacrifices were performed at Fenyin, they again sent General Who Cherishes Virtue Tuoluoli with bottle incense, ivory, amber, wumingyi, embroidered silk, red silk, green and yellow cotton, fine yuenuo, red camel hair, gold-threaded jade garments, green and white glass wine vessels, rose water, thousand-year jujubes, and the like.

sentences.zh: 詔令陪位，禮成，並賜冠帶服物。

translations.literal: An edict ordered them to take part in the ritual positions; when the rites were completed, all were granted caps, belts, and garments.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered them to take part in the ritual positions; when the rites were completed, all were granted caps, belts, and garments.

sentences.zh: 五年，廣州言大食國人無西忽盧華百三十歲，耳有重輪，貌甚偉異。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Guangzhou reported that a Dashi man named Wuxihulu was one hundred thirty years old, with double rings on his ears, and his appearance was very grand and unusual.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Guangzhou reported that a Dashi man named Wuxihulu was one hundred thirty years old, with double rings on his ears, and his appearance was very grand and unusual.

sentences.zh: 自言遠慕皇化，附古邏國舶船而來。

translations.literal: He stated of himself that from afar he admired the imperial transformation and came attached to a ship of the ancient Luo state.
translations.idiomatic: He stated that from afar he admired the imperial transformation and had come on a ship from the ancient Luo state.

sentences.zh: 詔就賜錦袍、銀帶加束帛。

translations.literal: An edict granted him on the spot a brocade robe, silver belt, and additional bundles of silk.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted him on the spot a brocade robe, a silver belt, and additional bundles of silk.

sentences.zh: 天禧三年，遣使蒲麻勿陁婆離、副使蒲加心等來貢。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianxi, they sent the envoy Pumawu Tuopoli, vice-envoy Pu Jiaxin, and others with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tianxi they sent the envoy Pumawu Tuopoli, vice-envoy Pu Jiaxin, and others with tribute.

sentences.zh: 先是，其入貢路繇沙州，涉夏國，抵秦州。

translations.literal: Previously their tribute route went by Shazhou, passed through the Xia state, and reached Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Previously their tribute route ran through Shazhou and Western Xia to Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 乾興初，趙德明請道其國中，不許。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianxing, Zhao Deming requested a route through his territory; this was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Qianxing, Zhao Deming asked that the route pass through his territory; the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 至天聖元年來貢，恐為西人鈔略，乃詔自今取海路繇廣州至京師。

translations.literal: When they came with tribute in the first year of Tiansheng, fearing plunder by the western peoples, an edict ordered that from then on they should take the sea route by Guangzhou to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When they came with tribute in the first year of Tiansheng, fearing raids by the western peoples, an edict ordered that henceforth they should travel by sea via Guangzhou to the capital.

sentences.zh: 至和、嘉祐間，四貢方物。

translations.literal: Between Zhihe and Jiayou they presented local products on four occasions.
translations.idiomatic: Between Zhihe and Jiayou they presented tribute on four occasions.

sentences.zh: 最後以其首領蒲沙乙為武寧司階。

translations.literal: Finally their leader Pu Shayi was made a rank in the Wuning Office.
translations.idiomatic: Finally their leader Pu Shayi was granted a rank in the Wuning Office.

sentences.zh: 熙寧中，其使辛押陀羅乞統察蕃長司公事，詔廣州裁度。

translations.literal: During the Xining era, their envoy Xinyatuoluo requested to be put in charge of the foreign chiefs' office affairs; an edict ordered Guangzhou to decide.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xining era their envoy Xinyatuoluo requested to be put in charge of the foreign chiefs' office affairs; an edict ordered Guangzhou to decide.

sentences.zh: 又進錢銀助修廣州城，不許。

translations.literal: He also presented money and silver to assist in repairing the Guangzhou city wall; this was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He also offered money and silver to assist in repairing the Guangzhou city wall; this was not permitted.

sentences.zh: 六年，都蕃首保順郎將蒲陀婆離慈表令男麻勿奉貢物，乞以自代，而求為將軍，詔但授麻勿郎將。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Chief Foreign Officer Bao Shun Langjiang Pu Tuoboli Ci submitted a memorial ordering his son Mawu to present tribute goods, begging to be replaced by himself and requesting appointment as general; an edict granted Mawu only the rank of Langjiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Chief Foreign Officer Bao Shun Langjiang Pu Tuoboli Ci submitted a memorial ordering his son Mawu to present tribute goods, begging to be replaced by himself and requesting appointment as general; an edict granted Mawu only the rank of Langjiang.

sentences.zh: 其國部屬各異名，故有勿巡，有陀婆離，有俞盧和地，有麻囉跋等國，然皆冠以大食。

translations.literal: The subordinate divisions of their country each had different names; hence there were Wuxun, Tuopoli, Yuluhedi, Maliba, and other states, yet all were crowned with the name Dashi.
translations.idiomatic: The subordinate divisions of their country each had different names; hence there were Wuxun, Tuopoli, Yuluhedi, Maliba, and other states, yet all were crowned with the name Dashi.

sentences.zh: 勿巡所貢，又有龍腦、兜羅錦、球錦袂、蕃花簟，陀婆有金飾壽帶、連環臂鉤、數珠之屬。

translations.literal: What Wuxun presented as tribute also included dragon's-brain camphor, douluo brocade, ball-brocade sleeves, and foreign flower mats; Tuopoli had gold-decorated longevity belts, linked arm hooks, prayer beads, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: What Wuxun presented as tribute also included dragon's-brain camphor, douluo brocade, ball-brocade sleeves, and foreign flower mats; Tuopoli had gold-decorated longevity belts, linked arm hooks, prayer beads, and the like.

sentences.zh: 政和中，橫州士曹蔡蒙休押伴其使入都，沿道故滯留，強市其香藥不償直。

translations.literal: During the Zhenghe era, Hengzhou Staff Assistant Cai Mengxiu, escorting their envoys to the capital, deliberately delayed along the route and forcibly purchased their incense and medicines without paying full value.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenghe era Hengzhou Staff Assistant Cai Mengxiu, escorting their envoys to the capital, deliberately delayed along the route and forcibly purchased their incense and medicines without paying full value.

sentences.zh: 事聞，詔提點刑獄置獄推治，因詔自今蕃夷入貢，並選承務郎以上清幹官押伴，按程而行，無故不得過一日，乞取賈市者論以自盜雲。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, an edict ordered the judicial intendant to set up a prison and investigate; an edict was also issued that from now on when barbarians and foreigners entered with tribute, officials of Registrar rank and above who were upright and capable should be chosen as escorts, proceeding according to schedule, not exceeding one day without cause; those who begged to buy and trade would be prosecuted as self-thieves.
translations.idiomatic: When the matter was reported, an edict ordered the judicial intendant to set up a prison and investigate; an edict was also issued that from now on when barbarians and foreigners entered with tribute, officials of Registrar rank and above who were upright and capable should be chosen as escorts, proceeding according to schedule without exceeding one day without cause; those who begged to buy and trade would be prosecuted as self-thieves.

sentences.zh: 其國在泉州西北，舟行四十餘日至藍里。

translations.literal: Their country lies northwest of Quanzhou; by boat forty-odd days reach Lanli.
translations.idiomatic: Their country lies northwest of Quanzhou; by boat it is forty-odd days to Lanli.

sentences.zh: 次年乘風颿，又六十餘日始達其國。

translations.literal: The next year, riding favorable winds and sails, another sixty-odd days before reaching their country.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, riding favorable winds, another sixty-odd days are required before reaching their country.

sentences.zh: 地雄壯廣袤，民俗侈麗，甲於諸蕃，天氣多寒。

translations.literal: The land is powerful, vast, and broad; the people's customs are extravagant and splendid, foremost among all foreign states; the weather is mostly cold.
translations.idiomatic: The land is powerful, vast, and broad; the people's customs are extravagant and splendid, foremost among all foreign states; the weather is mostly cold.

sentences.zh: 其王錦衣玉帶，躡金履，朔望冠百寶純金冠。

translations.literal: Their king wears brocade robes and jade belts, treads gold shoes, and on the first and fifteenth of the month wears a pure gold crown set with a hundred treasures.
translations.idiomatic: Their king wears brocade robes and jade belts, treads gold shoes, and on the first and fifteenth of the month wears a pure gold crown set with a hundred treasures.

sentences.zh: 其居以碼磠為柱，綠甘為壁，水晶為瓦，碌石為磚，活石為灰，帷幕用百花錦。

translations.literal: His dwelling uses marble as pillars, green sweet as walls, crystal as tiles, green stone as bricks, living stone as mortar, and curtains of hundred-flower brocade.
translations.idiomatic: His dwelling uses marble as pillars, green sweet as walls, crystal as tiles, green stone as bricks, living stone as mortar, and curtains of hundred-flower brocade.

sentences.zh: 官有丞相、太尉，各領兵馬二萬餘人。

translations.literal: Officials include a chief minister and a grand marshal, each commanding more than twenty thousand troops and horses.
translations.idiomatic: Officials include a chief minister and a grand marshal, each commanding more than twenty thousand troops and horses.

sentences.zh: 馬高七尺，士卒驍勇。

translations.literal: Horses stand seven feet high; soldiers and officers are fierce and brave.
translations.idiomatic: Horses stand seven feet high; soldiers and officers are fierce and brave.

sentences.zh: 民居屋宇略與中國同。

translations.literal: The people's dwellings and buildings are roughly the same as in China.
translations.idiomatic: The people's dwellings and buildings are roughly the same as in China.

sentences.zh: 市肆多金銀綾錦。

translations.literal: Markets and shops have much gold, silver, silk, and brocade.
translations.idiomatic: Markets and shops have much gold, silver, silk, and brocade.

sentences.zh: 工匠技術，咸精其能。

translations.literal: Craftsmen's skills all excel in their arts.
translations.idiomatic: Craftsmen's skills all excel in their arts.

sentences.zh: 建炎三年，遣使奉寶玉珠貝入貢。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianyan, they sent envoys presenting precious jade, pearls, and cowries as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jianyan they sent envoys presenting precious jade, pearls, and cowries as tribute.

sentences.zh: 帝謂侍臣曰：「大觀、宣和間，茶馬之政廢，故武備不修，致金人亂華，危亡不絕如線。

translations.literal: The emperor said to his attending officials: "During the Daguan and Xuanhe eras, the tea-and-horse policy was abandoned, so military preparations were not maintained, causing the Jurchens to disrupt China and placing survival in unbroken peril like a thread.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to his attending officials: "During the Daguan and Xuanhe eras the tea-and-horse policy was abandoned, so military preparations were not maintained, causing the Jurchens to disrupt China and placing survival in unbroken peril like a thread.

sentences.zh: 今復捐數十萬緡以易無用之珠玉，曷若惜財以養戰士？」

translations.literal: Now again to spend several hundred thousand strings of cash to exchange for useless pearls and jade — how does that compare with cherishing wealth to support warriors?"
translations.idiomatic: Now again to spend several hundred thousand strings of cash to exchange for useless pearls and jade — how does that compare with cherishing wealth to support warriors?"

sentences.zh: 詔張浚卻之，優賜以答遠人之意。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Zhang Jun to decline them, yet generously grant gifts in reply to the sentiments of the distant people.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Zhang Jun to decline them, yet generously grant gifts in reply to the sentiments of the distant people.

sentences.zh: 紹興元年，復遣使貢文犀、象齒，朝廷亦厚加賜與，而不貪其利。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaoxing, they again sent envoys with patterned rhinoceros horn and ivory tusks; the court also generously granted gifts and did not covet their profit.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shaoxing they again sent envoys with patterned rhinoceros horn and ivory tusks; the court also generously granted gifts and did not covet their profit.

sentences.zh: 故遠人懷之，而貢賦不絕。

translations.literal: Therefore distant people cherished this, and tribute did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore distant people cherished this, and tribute did not cease.

sentences.zh: 層檀國在南海傍，城距海二十里。

translations.literal: The Cengtan state is beside the Southern Sea; its city is twenty li from the sea.
translations.idiomatic: The state of Cengtan lies beside the Southern Sea; its city is twenty li from the sea.

sentences.zh: 熙寧四年始入貢。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xining it first entered tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Xining it first sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 海道便風行百六十日，經勿巡、古林、三佛齊國乃至廣州。

translations.literal: By sea route with favorable winds it is one hundred sixty days, passing Wuxun, Gulin, and Sanfoqi to reach Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: By sea route with favorable winds it is one hundred sixty days, passing Wuxun, Gulin, and Sanfoqi to reach Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 其王名亞美羅亞眉蘭，傳國五百年，十世矣。

translations.literal: Their king is named Yameiluoyameilan; the state has been transmitted five hundred years, ten generations.
translations.idiomatic: Their king is named Yameiluoyameilan; the state has been transmitted five hundred years across ten generations.

sentences.zh: 人語音如大食。

translations.literal: The people's speech sounds like Dashi.
translations.idiomatic: The people's speech sounds like Dashi.

sentences.zh: 地春冬暖。

translations.literal: The land is warm in spring and winter.
translations.idiomatic: The land is warm in spring and winter.

sentences.zh: 貴人以越布纏頭，服花錦白氎布，出入乘象、馬。

translations.literal: Nobles wrap their heads in yue cloth and wear flowered brocade and white felt; going out they ride elephants and horses.
translations.idiomatic: Nobles wrap their heads in yue cloth and wear flowered brocade and white felt; going out they ride elephants and horses.

sentences.zh: 有奉祿。

translations.literal: They have stipends.
translations.idiomatic: They receive stipends.

sentences.zh: 其法輕罪杖，重罪死。

translations.literal: Their law: light offenses are punished with the staff; heavy offenses with death.
translations.idiomatic: Their law punishes light offenses with the staff and heavy offenses with death.

sentences.zh: 穀有稻、粟、麥。

translations.literal: Grains include rice, millet, and wheat.
translations.idiomatic: Grains include rice, millet, and wheat.

sentences.zh: 食有魚。

translations.literal: Food includes fish.
translations.idiomatic: Food includes fish.

sentences.zh: 畜有綿羊、山羊、沙牛、水牛、橐駝、馬、犀、象。

translations.literal: Livestock includes sheep, goats, sand oxen, water buffalo, camels, horses, rhinoceros, and elephants.
translations.idiomatic: Livestock includes sheep, goats, sand oxen, water buffalo, camels, horses, rhinoceros, and elephants.

sentences.zh: 藥有木香、血竭、沒藥、鵬砂、阿魏、薰陸。

translations.literal: Medicines include costusroot, dragon's blood, myrrh, borax, asafetida, and frankincense.
translations.idiomatic: Medicines include costusroot, dragon's blood, myrrh, borax, asafetida, and frankincense.

sentences.zh: 產真珠、玻璃、密沙華三酒。

translations.literal: It produces pearls, glass, and three wines, including mishahua.
translations.idiomatic: Its products include pearls, glass, and three wines, among them mishahua.

sentences.zh: 交易用錢，官自鑄，三分其齊，金銅相半，而銀居一分，禁民私鑄。

translations.literal: For exchange they use money, minted by the government itself; the alloy is divided in three parts, gold and copper half and half, while silver occupies one part; private minting by the people is forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Trade was conducted with currency minted solely by the state: the alloy was divided in thirds, with gold and copper in equal measure and silver making up the remaining third. Private coinage was forbidden.

sentences.zh: 元豐六年，使保順郎將層伽尼再至，神宗念其絕遠，詔頒齎如故事，仍加賜白金二千兩。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yuanfeng, the envoy Bao Shun Langjiang Cenggani came again; Emperor Shenzong, mindful of their extreme distance, ordered bestowal of gifts according to precedent, and additionally granted two thousand taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Yuanfeng the envoy Cenggani, a Bao Shun Langjiang, returned to court. Mindful of the vast distance they had traveled, Emperor Shenzong ordered gifts awarded according to established precedent and added a further grant of two thousand taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 龜茲本回鶻別種。

translations.literal: Kucha was originally a separate branch of the Huihe.
translations.idiomatic: Kucha was originally an offshoot of the Uyghurs.

sentences.zh: 其國主自稱師子王，衣黃衣，寶冠，與宰相九人同治國事。

translations.literal: Its king styled himself Lion King, wore yellow robes and a jeweled crown, and together with nine chancellors jointly administered state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler styled himself the Lion King, dressed in yellow robes and a jeweled crown, and governed jointly with nine chancellors.

sentences.zh: 國城有市井而無錢貨，以花蕊布博易。

translations.literal: The capital had markets but no currency; they bartered using flowered-pistil cloth.
translations.idiomatic: The capital had marketplaces but no coinage; trade was conducted in flowered calico.

sentences.zh: 有米麥瓜果。

translations.literal: They had rice, wheat, and melons and fruits.
translations.idiomatic: Rice, wheat, melons, and fruit were grown there.

sentences.zh: 西至大食國行六十日，東至夏州九十日。

translations.literal: Westward to the Dashi state was sixty days' travel; eastward to Xiazhou ninety days.
translations.idiomatic: It lay sixty days' journey west of the Arab lands and ninety days east of Xiazhou.

sentences.zh: 或稱西州回鶻，或稱西州龜茲，又稱龜茲回鶻。

translations.literal: It was sometimes called Xizhou Huihe, sometimes Xizhou Kucha, and again Kucha Huihe.
translations.idiomatic: It was known variously as the Xizhou Uyghurs, Xizhou Kucha, and Kucha Uyghurs.

sentences.zh: 自天聖至景祐四年，入貢者五，最後賜以佛經一藏。

translations.literal: From Tiansheng through the fourth year of Jingyou, tribute was sent five times; lastly they were granted one complete Buddhist canon.
translations.idiomatic: From the Tiansheng era through the fourth year of Jingyou they sent tribute five times; on the last occasion they were granted a complete set of Buddhist scriptures.

sentences.zh: 熙寧四年，使李延慶、曹福入貢。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xining, envoys Li Yanqing and Cao Fu entered tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Xining envoys Li Yanqing and Cao Fu came with tribute.

sentences.zh: 五年，又使盧大明、篤都入貢。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, again envoys Lu Daming and Dudu entered tribute.
translations.idiomatic: The following year envoys Lu Daming and Dudu were sent with tribute.

sentences.zh: 紹聖三年，使大首領阿連撒羅等三人以表章及玉佛至洮西。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shaosheng, three men led by the great chieftain Aliansaluo brought a memorial and a jade Buddha to the west of Tao.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Shaosheng the grand chieftain Aliansaluo and two others arrived on the Tao River frontier with a memorial and a jade Buddha.

sentences.zh: 熙河經略使以其罕通使，請令於熙、秦州博買，而估所齎物價答賜遣還，從之。

translations.literal: The Xifu circuit commissioner, because they rarely sent envoys, requested that they be allowed to purchase at Xizhou and Qinzhou and be recompensed according to the appraised value of what they had brought, then sent back; this was approved.
translations.idiomatic: Because their embassies were rare, the Xifu frontier commissioner asked that they be received for government purchase at Xizhou and Qinzhou, paid the appraised value of their goods, and sent home; the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 沙州本漢敦煌故地，唐天寶末陷於西戎。

translations.literal: Shazhou was originally the former Han territory of Dunhuang; at the end of Tianbao of Tang it fell to the Western Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Shazhou was the old Han seat of Dunhuang; at the close of the Tianbao era it was lost to the Western barbarians.

sentences.zh: 大中五年，張義潮以州歸順，詔建沙州為歸義軍，以義潮為節度使，領河沙甘肅伊西等州觀察、營田處置使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Dazhong, Zhang Yichao submitted the prefecture in allegiance; an edict established Shazhou as the Guiyi Army, appointing Yichao military commissioner and also commissioner for observation and agriculture of He, Sha, Gan, Su, Yi, Xi, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Dazhong Zhang Yichao brought the region back to Tang allegiance. The court established the Guiyi Army at Shazhou, made Yichao its military commissioner, and charged him with observation and agricultural administration over He, Sha, Gan, Su, Yi, Xi, and neighboring prefectures.

sentences.zh: 義潮入朝，以從子淮深領州事。

translations.literal: When Yichao went to court, his nephew's son Huaishen was left to oversee prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Yichao traveled to court, his grand-nephew Huaishen was left in charge of the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 至朱梁時，張氏之後絕，州人推長史曹義金為帥。

translations.literal: By the time of Later Liang, Zhang's posterity was extinct, and the people of the prefecture raised Chief Clerk Cao Yijin as commander.
translations.idiomatic: By the Later Liang period the Zhang line had died out, and the people elevated chief clerk Cao Yijin as their leader.

sentences.zh: 義金卒，子元忠嗣。

translations.literal: Yijin died; his son Yuanzhong succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Yijin died and was succeeded by his son Yuanzhong.

sentences.zh: 周顯德二年來貢，授本軍節度、檢校太尉、同中書門下平章事，鑄印賜之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xiande of Zhou they came to tribute; he was appointed commissioner of this army, honorary grand general, and co-administrator of affairs under the Secretariat-Chancellery, and a seal was cast and granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Later Zhou Xiande they sent tribute. Yuanzhong was appointed military commissioner of the Guiyi Army, honorary Grand General, and ceremonial co-grand councillor, and a seal was cast and bestowed upon him.

sentences.zh: 建隆三年加兼中書令，子延恭為瓜州防禦使。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianlong he was further made concurrent Zhongshu Ling; his son Yangong was made defender of Guazhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jianlong he was further named concurrent Director of the Secretariat; his son Yangong was appointed defender of Guazhou.

sentences.zh: 興國五年元忠卒，子延祿遣人來貢。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xingguo Yuanzhong died; his son Yanlu sent men to enter tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Xingguo Yuanzhong died; his son Yanlu dispatched envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 贈元忠敦煌郡王，授延祿本軍節度，弟延晟為瓜州刺史，延瑞為衙內都虞候。

translations.literal: Yuanzhong was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Dunhuang Commandery; Yanlu was appointed military commissioner of this army; his younger brothers Yancheng as prefect of Guazhou and Yanrui as chief commander of the inner guards.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhong was posthumously enfeoffed Prince of Dunhuang; Yanlu became military commissioner of the Guiyi Army, his brother Yancheng was made prefect of Guazhou, and Yanrui chief commander of the inner guards.

sentences.zh: 咸平四年，封延祿為譙郡王。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xianping, Yanlu was enfeoffed as Prince of Qiao Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Xianping Yanlu was enfeoffed Prince of Qiao.

sentences.zh: 五年，延祿、延瑞為從子宗壽所害，宗壽權知留後，而以其弟宗允權知瓜州。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Yanlu and Yanrui were killed by their nephew's son Zongshou; Zongshou provisionally served as acting chief administrator, and his younger brother Zongyun provisionally governed Guazhou.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Yanlu and Yanrui were murdered by their grand-nephew Zongshou, who assumed acting control as chief administrator and left his brother Zongyun to govern Guazhou.

sentences.zh: 表求旌節，乃授宗壽節度使，宗允檢校尚書左僕射、知瓜州，宗壽子賢順為衙內都指揮使。

translations.literal: He memorialized requesting the envoy staff of office; then Zongshou was appointed military commissioner, Zongyun made honorary Left Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing and administrator of Guazhou, and Zongshou's son Xianshun chief commander of the inner guards.
translations.idiomatic: Zongshou petitioned for formal commission; the court appointed him military commissioner, made Zongyun honorary Left Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing and administrator of Guazhou, and named Zongshou's son Xianshun chief commander of the inner guards.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符末宗壽卒，授賢順本軍節度，弟延惠為檢校刑部尚書、知瓜州。

translations.literal: At the end of Dazhong Xiangfu Zongshou died; Xianshun was appointed military commissioner of this army, and his younger brother Yanhui honorary Minister of Punishments and administrator of Guazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Dazhong Xiangfu era Zongshou died. Xianshun was appointed military commissioner of the Guiyi Army, and his brother Yanhui honorary Minister of Punishments and administrator of Guazhou.

sentences.zh: 賢順表乞金字藏經洎茶藥金箔，詔賜之。

translations.literal: Xianshun memorialized begging a gold-letter sutra canon together with tea, medicines, and gold leaf; an edict granted them.
translations.idiomatic: Xianshun petitioned for a gold-letter Buddhist canon, tea, medicines, and gold leaf; the court granted his request.

sentences.zh: 至天聖初，遣使來謝，貢乳香、硇砂、玉團。

translations.literal: By the beginning of Tiansheng, he sent envoys to give thanks, presenting frankincense, sal ammoniac, and jade lumps.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Tiansheng era he sent envoys to express thanks, offering frankincense, sal ammoniac, and worked jade.

sentences.zh: 自景祐至皇祐中，凡七貢方物。

translations.literal: From Jingyou through the Huangyou era, altogether seven times they sent tribute of local products.
translations.idiomatic: From Jingyou through Huangyou they sent tribute seven times.

sentences.zh: 拂菻國東南至滅力沙，北至海，皆四十程。

translations.literal: The Fulin state: southeast to Mielisha forty stages, north to the sea forty stages.
translations.idiomatic: The land of Byzantium extended forty days' journey southeast to Mielisha and forty days north to the sea.

sentences.zh: 西至海三十程。
