translations.literal: West to the sea thirty stages.
translations.idiomatic: To the west the sea lay thirty days away.

sentences.zh: 東自西大食及于闐、回紇、青唐，乃抵中國。

translations.literal: Eastward from Western Dashi and through Yutian, Huihe, and Qingtang one then reached China.
translations.idiomatic: Eastward one passed through the Western Arabs, Khotan, the Uyghurs, and Qingtang before reaching China.

sentences.zh: 歷代未嘗朝貢。

translations.literal: Through successive dynasties they never once sent tribute.
translations.idiomatic: No dynasty had ever received tribute from them.

sentences.zh: 元豐四年十月，其王滅力伊靈改撒始遣大首領你廝都令廝孟判來獻鞍馬、刀劍、真珠，言其國地甚寒，土屋無瓦。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the fourth year of Yuanfeng, its king Mieliyiling Gaisa first dispatched the great chieftain Nisudoulingsimengpan to present saddles and horses, swords, and pearls, stating that their land was very cold and earthen houses had no tiles.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the fourth year of Yuanfeng King Mieliyiling Gaisa of Byzantium sent his grand chieftain Nisudoulingsimengpan with saddled horses, swords, and pearls—the first mission from his court. The envoys reported that their country was bitterly cold and even houses were earthen, without tile roofs.

sentences.zh: 產金、銀、珠、西錦、牛、羊、馬、獨峰駝、梨、杏、千年棗、巴欖、粟、麥，以蒲萄釀酒。

translations.literal: It produced gold, silver, pearls, Western brocade, cattle, sheep, horses, one-humped camels, pears, apricots, thousand-year jujubes, olives, millet, and wheat; wine was brewed from grapes.
translations.idiomatic: The realm yielded gold, silver, pearls, Western brocade, cattle, sheep, horses, one-humped camels, pears, apricots, thousand-year jujubes, olives, millet, and wheat; grapes were fermented into wine.

sentences.zh: 樂有箜篌、壺琴、小篳篥、偏鼓。

translations.literal: In music there were konghou, hu qin, small bili, and side drums.
translations.idiomatic: Their music featured the konghou, hu qin, small pipe, and side drum.

sentences.zh: 王服紅黃衣，以金線織絲布纏頭，歲三月則詣佛寺，坐紅床，使人舁之。

translations.literal: The king wore red and yellow robes, wrapped his head in gold-thread woven silk cloth; each year in the third month he went to a Buddhist temple, sat on a red couch, and had men carry him.
translations.idiomatic: The king dressed in red and yellow robes with a gold-thread silk turban. Each year in the third month he went to a Buddhist temple, where he was seated on a red couch and borne aloft by attendants.

sentences.zh: 貴臣如王之服，或青綠、緋白、粉紅、褐紫，並纏頭跨馬。

translations.literal: Noble ministers dressed like the king, in blue-green, crimson-white, pink, or brown-purple, all wrapping their heads and riding horseback.
translations.idiomatic: Great officers dressed like the king in blue-green, crimson and white, pink, or brown and purple, all with wrapped heads and mounted on horseback.

sentences.zh: 城市田野，皆有首領主之，每歲惟夏秋兩得奉，給金、錢、錦、穀、帛，以治事大小為差。

translations.literal: In cities and countryside, all had chiefs who held authority; each year they received stipends only in summer and autumn twice, granted gold, money, brocade, grain, and silk, according to the size of their affairs as the distinction.
translations.idiomatic: City and countryside alike were ruled by chiefs who received stipends only twice a year, in summer and autumn—paid in gold, coin, brocade, grain, and silk according to the importance of their offices.

sentences.zh: 刑罰罪輕者杖數十，重者至二百，大罪則盛以毛囊投諸海。

translations.literal: Punishments: for light crimes flogging of several tens; for heavy up to two hundred; for great crimes one was packed in a fur sack and cast into the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Penalties ranged from dozens of strokes of the rod for minor offenses to as many as two hundred for grave ones; capital crimes were punished by sewing the guilty into a fur sack and throwing them into the sea.

sentences.zh: 不尚鬥戰，鄰國小有爭，但以文字來往相詰問，事大亦出兵。

translations.literal: They did not esteem battle; when neighboring states had small disputes, they merely exchanged written messages to question one another; for great matters they also sent out troops.
translations.idiomatic: They did not favor warfare: minor quarrels with neighbors were settled by exchange of written dispatches, though major disputes could still bring armies into the field.

sentences.zh: 鑄金銀為錢，無穿孔，麵鑿彌勒佛，背為王名，禁民私造。

translations.literal: Gold and silver were cast into money without holes pierced; the face was carved with Maitreya Buddha, the reverse bore the king's name; private manufacture by the people was forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: They minted coin from gold and silver without a central hole: Maitreya Buddha on the obverse, the king's name on the reverse. Private minting was forbidden.

sentences.zh: 元祐六年，其使兩至。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yuanyou, their envoys came twice.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Yuanyou two embassies arrived from their court.

sentences.zh: 詔別賜其王帛二百匹、白金瓶、襲衣、金束帶。

translations.literal: An edict separately bestowed on their king two hundred bolts of silk, a silver bottle, a robe of office, and a gold girdle.
translations.idiomatic: The court separately bestowed upon their king two hundred bolts of silk, a silver vessel, a ceremonial robe, and a gold belt.
